He was proposing to stay down at Lincote alone for a month or so, and would then turn on to the new page.

===Chinese===
那天早晨，我在《泰晤士报》（*Times*）那些更为庄重的版面上没找到什么重大的新闻，于是，仅仅因为懒得动弹、不愿着手去办那一大堆等着我的事，我翻到头版，从第七栏开始，煞有介事地对着“招聘”栏琢磨起来，心里盼着那位“爱好游戏的淑女”——她正谋求一份家庭女教师的职位——能找到正合心意的事。我扫了一眼各类学术团体主办的讲座启事，暗自庆幸既不必去讲、也不必去听其中任何一场。我推敲起“商业良机”一栏；又徒劳地想去猜想那些神秘的“个人启事”短笺里藏着什么线索，便仍这么横着、像螃蟹似的翻阅，翻到了“讣告续编”。

在那儿，我猛地一怔：西比尔·罗克（Sybil Rorke），已故厄内斯特·罗克爵士（Sir Ernest Rorke）的遗孀，已于托基（Torquay）猝然辞世，年仅三十二岁。关于一位曾经那样声名显赫、光彩照人的女子，竟只有这么一则光秃秃的通告，这似乎有些蹊跷；我翻到讣告栏细看，才发现自己方才漫不经心的浏览，竟在那里漏掉了一段表达敬意与惋惜的文字。她在睡梦中死去，并已宣布将进行死因研讯。这么看来，我方才的慵懒倒也派上了些用场，因为阿奇·罗克（Archie Rorke）——厄内斯特爵士的远房表弟，却又是其产业与爵位的继承人——今晚会到乡间来与我小住几日，我能在见到他之前先知晓此事，倒也欣慰。这事会对他有多大影响，或者到底会不会影响他，我全然无从揣想。

这真是一桩扑朔迷离的事！我想，如今罗克夫人既已辞世，除了他，怕再没人知道其中的始末了。如果还有人知道，那本该是我，然而阿奇——我最老的朋友，我本要做他的伴郎的人——却从未向我吐露过半个字的解释。事实上，我所知的，并不比世人所知的多出一丝一毫，即：厄内斯特·罗克爵士去世一年后，其遗孀与新封的准男爵阿奇博尔德·罗克爵士（Sir Archibald Rorke）订婚的消息公之于世；而就在原定婚期前两周，却又简短地宣布婚礼将不再举行。我见报后打电话给阿奇，却被告知他已离开伦敦；几天后他从林科特（Lincote）——汉普郡（Hampshire）的那处地方，他是从表兄那里继承的——给我来信说，关于他解除婚约一事，除了“确有其事”之外，他无可奉告。整件——他原本写了一个词，又细心地涂掉了——“这桩事”，如今已是从他生命里裁去的一页。他打算独自在林科特住上一个月光景，然后再翻到新的一页去。

===Original===
Lady Rorke, so I heard, had also left London immediately and passed the summer in Italy. Then she took a furnished house in Torquay, where she lived for the remainder of the year which intervened between the breaking off of her engagement and her death. She cut herself completely off from all her friends﻿—and no woman, surely, ever commanded a larger host of them﻿—saw nobody, seldom went outside her house and garden, and observed the same unbroken silence as did Archie about what had happened. And now, with all her youth and charm and beauty, she had gone down dumb into the Great Silence.

===Chinese===
听说罗克夫人也立即离开了伦敦，到意大利度过了那个夏天。随后她在托基租下一所带家具的宅子，从解除婚约到她去世之间那一年余下的时日，便住在那里。她与所有的朋友都断绝了往来——天底下怕再没有哪个女人拥有比她更多的朋友——她不见任何人，极少走出那宅子和花园，并且和阿奇一样，对所发生的事保持着同样丝毫不漏的缄默。而如今，带着她全部的青春、魅力与美貌，她哑口无言地沉入了那永恒的大静默之中。

===Original===
With the prospect of seeing Archie that evening it was no wonder that the thought of Lady Rorke ran all day in my head like a tune heard long ago which now recalled itself to my mind in scattered staves of melody. Meetings and talks with her, phrase by phrase, reconstructed themselves, and as these memories grew definite and complete I found that, even as before, when I was actually experiencing them, there lurked underneath the gay rhythms and joyousness something macabre and mysterious. Today that was accentuated, whereas before when I listened for it, trying to isolate it from the rest and so perhaps dispel it, it was always overscored by some triumphant crescendo: her presence diverted eye and ear alike. Yet such a simile halts; perhaps, still in simile, I shall more accurately define this underlying “something” by saying that her presence was like some gorgeous rosebush, full of flowers, and sun, and sweetness; then, even as one admired and applauded and inhaled, one saw that among its buds and blossoms there emerged the spikes of some other plant, bitter and poisonous, but growing from the same soil as the rose, and intertwined with it. But immediately a fresh glory met your eye, a fresh fragrance enchanted you.

===Chinese===
想到今晚会见到阿奇，也就难怪一整天里，罗克夫人的影子都在我脑子里萦回，像一支很久以前听见过的曲子，此刻零零散散地、一节节旋律地重新浮现到心头。与她的一次次会面、一次次交谈，一句一句地在脑中重现；随着这些记忆渐渐清晰、完整起来，我发觉，正如当初亲身经历时一样，在那轻快的节奏与欢乐之下，仍潜伏着某种阴森而诡秘的东西。今日这一点被凸显了出来，而在从前，每当我刻意去捕捉它，想把它从其余部分里分离出来从而或许驱散它时，它又总是被某一节辉煌的渐强所盖过：有她在场，耳目便都被引开了。然而这种比喻终究不贴切；或许，仍沿用比喻，我能更准确地界定这潜伏的“某物”：她在场，好比一丛华丽的蔷薇，满是花朵、满是阳光、满是甜美；随后，就在你欣赏、赞叹、深嗅之际，你却看见，在它的花蕾与花朵之间，钻出了另一种植物的尖刺，又苦又毒，却与蔷薇同根而生，与它缠绕在一起。可紧接着，又有新的光彩扑入你的眼帘，新的芬芳令你神迷。

===Original===
As I rummaged among my memories of her, certain scenes which significantly illustrated this curiously vivid impression stirred and made themselves manifest to me, and now they were not broken in upon by her presence. One such occurred on the first evening that I ever met her, which was in the summer before the death of her husband. The moment that she entered the room where we were waiting before dinner for her arrival, the stale, sultry air of a June evening grew fresh and effervescent; never have I come across so radiant and infectious a vitality. She was tall and big, with the splendour of the Juno-type, and though she was then close on thirty, the iridescence of girlhood was still hers. Without effort she Pied-pipered a rather stodgy party to dance to her flutings, she caused everyone to become silly and pleased and full of laughter. At her bidding we indulged in ridiculous games, dumb-crambo, and whatnot, and after that the carpet was rolled up and we capered to the strains of a gramophone. And then the incident occurred.

I was standing with her, for a breath of air, on the balcony outside the drawing-room windows which faced the park. She had just made a great curtsey to a slip of the moon that rose above the trees and had borrowed a shilling of me in order to turn it.

===Chinese===
我在记忆里翻寻着关于她的往事，有几幕恰好印证了这种奇特而鲜明印象的情景，便浮了上来、显现眼前，而此刻，它们不再被她在场所打断。其中一幕，发生在我初次与她见面的那个晚上，那是她丈夫去世前的一个夏天。她一走进那间屋子——晚餐前我们正在那里等她到来——六月黄昏里那股沉闷湿热的空气，立刻变得清新而活跃起来；我从未见过如此光彩照人、如此富于感染力的勃勃生机。她身材高挑、体态丰盈，带着朱诺式（the Juno-type）的那种华贵气度，虽说她那时已将近三十岁，少女时代那种斑斓的光彩却仍属于她。她毫不费力地，像花衣魔笛手（the Pied Piper）一般，引得那一屋子本有些沉闷的客人，都随着她的笛声跳起舞来；她让每一个人都变得傻乎乎、乐陶陶、满心欢笑。在她的提议下，我们玩起种种荒唐的游戏，什么哑谜字谜（dumb-crambo）啦，什么名目繁多的把戏啦，再后来，地毯被卷了起来，我们随着留声机的乐曲蹦蹦跳跳。就在这时，那件事发生了。

我和她一同站在起居室窗外那个面朝园林的阳台上，透一口气。她刚刚对着树梢上方那一弯新月郑重其事地行了一个屈膝礼，又向我借了一先令，好把它转一转。

===Original===
“No, I can’t swear that I believe in moon-luck,” she said, “but after all it does no harm, and, in case it’s true, you can’t afford to make an enemy of her. Ah, what’s that?”

A thrush, attracted by the lights inside, had flown between us, dashed itself against the window, and now lay fluttering on the ground at our feet. Instantly she was all pity and tenderness. She picked up the bird, examined it, and found that its wing was broken.

“Ah, poor thing!” she said. “Look, its wing-bone is snapped; the end protrudes. And how terrified it is! What are we to do?”

It was clear that the kindest thing to do would be to put the bird out of its pain, but when I suggested that, she took a step back from me, and covered it with her other hand. Her eyes gleamed, her mouth smiled, and I saw the tip of her tongue swiftly pass over her lips as if licking them.

“No, that would be a terrible thing to do,” she said. “I shall take it home with me ever so carefully, and watch over it. I am afraid it is badly hurt. But it may live.”

Suddenly﻿—perhaps it was that swift licking of her lips that suggested the thought to me﻿—I felt instinctively that she was not so much pitiful as pleased. She stood there with eyes fixed on it, as it feebly struggled in her hands.

And then her face clouded; over its brightness there came a look of displeasure, of annoyance.

“I’m afraid it is dying,” she said. “Its poor frightened eyes are closing.”

The bird fluttered once more, then its legs stretched themselves stiffly out, and it lay still. She tossed it out of her hands on to the paved balcony, with a little shrug of her shoulders.

“What a fuss over a bird,” she said. “It was silly of it to fly against the glass. But I have too soft a heart; I cannot bear that the poor creatures should die. Let us go in and have one more romp. Oh, here is your shilling; I hope it will have brought me good luck. And then I must get home. My husband﻿—do you know him?﻿—always sits up till I get back, and he will scold me for being so late!”

===Chinese===
「不，我不能说自己信月亮带来的运气，」她说，「可话说回来，这反正也无害；况且，万一真是灵验的呢，你总不好去跟月亮结仇呀。哎呀，那是什么？」

一只画眉，被屋子里的灯光所吸引，从我们之间飞了进来，一头撞在窗玻璃上，此刻正扑棱着翅膀，掉在我们脚边的地上。她立时满脸怜惜与温柔。她拾起那只鸟，仔细查看，发现它的翅膀折了。

「哎呀，可怜的小东西！」她说，「你瞧，翅膀的骨头折了，断头都戳出来了。它吓成什么样了！我们该怎么办呢？」

很显然，最仁慈的做法是了结这只鸟的痛苦，可当我这么提议时，她却朝我退后一步，用另一只手把它护住了。她两眼放光，嘴角含笑，我看见她舌尖飞快地在嘴唇上舔了一下，仿佛在舔着自己的嘴唇。

「不，那可太残忍了，」她说，「我要把它小心翼翼地带回家去，好好照看。我怕它伤得不轻。可也许还能活。」

猛然间——也许是她那飞快的一舔，使我想起了这个念头——我本能地觉得，她与其说是在怜悯，不如说是在欢喜。她站在那里，两眼盯着它，看它在她手中无力地挣动。

接着，她的脸色阴沉下来；在那份明朗之上，掠过了一丝不悦、一丝恼怒的神情。

「我怕它要死了，」她说，「它那双可怜的、惊恐的小眼睛，正在阖上。」

那鸟又扑棱了一下，接着两腿直挺挺地伸了出去，便一动不动了。她把它往铺了石板的阳台地上一扔，微微耸了耸肩。

「为一只鸟这么大惊小怪，」她说，「它自己傻，偏要往玻璃上撞。可我心肠太软；受不了眼看着这些可怜的小生灵死去。咱们进去，再闹一回吧。哦，这是你的先令；但愿它给我带来了好运。然后我就得回家了。我丈夫——你认识他吗？——总要熬到我回来才睡，他又要嫌我回来得这么晚了！」

===Original===
There, then, was my first meeting with her, and there, too, were the spikes of the poisonous plant pushing up among the magnificence of her roses. And yet, so I thought to myself then, and so I think to myself now, I perhaps was utterly wrong about it all, in thus attributing to her a secret glee of which she was wholly incapable. So, with a certain effort I wiped the impression I had received off my mind, determining to consider myself quite mistaken. But, involuntarily, my mind as if to justify itself in having delineated such a picture, proceeded to delineate another.

===Chinese===
这便是我与她的第一次相见，也正是在那里，那些毒草的尖刺，从她那片华美的蔷薇之中冒了出来。然而，我那时是这么想，如今也还是这么想：也许我对此事全盘都错了，如此把一种她绝不可能怀有的隐秘快意归到她头上。于是，我费了点力气，把所得到的那印象从心里抹去，决心认定自己是大错特错了。可是，不由自主地，我的心——仿佛要为它所勾勒的这样一幅画像自辩似的——接着又勾勒出了另一幅。

===Original===
Very shortly after that first meeting I received from her a charming note, asking me to dine with her on a date not far distant. I telephoned a delighted acceptance, for, indeed, I wanted then, even as I did this morning, to convince myself that I was wholly in error concerning my interpretation of that incident concerning the thrush. Though I hold that no man has the right to accept the hospitality offered by one he does not like, in all points except one I admired and liked Lady Rorke immensely and wished to get rid of that one. So I gratefully accepted, and then hurried out on a dismal and overdue visit to the dentist’s. In the waiting-room was a girl of about twelve, with a hand nursing a rueful face, and from time to time she stifled a sob of pain or apprehension. I was just wondering whether it would be a breach of waiting-room etiquette to attempt to administer comfort or supply diversion, when the door opened and in came Lady Rorke. She laughed delightfully when she saw me.

“Hurrah! You’re another occupant of the condemned cell,” she said, “and very soon we shall both be sent for to the scaffold. I can’t describe to you what a coward I am about it. Why haven’t we got beaks like birds?﻿—”

Her glance fell on the forlorn little figure by the window, with the rueful face and the wet eyes.

“Why, here’s another of us,” she said. “And have they sent you to the dentist’s all alone, my dear?”

“Y﻿—yes.”

“How horrid of them!” said Lady Rorke. “They’ve sent me alone, too, and I think it’s most unfeeling. But you shan’t be alone, anyhow, I’ll come in with you, and sit by you, if you like that, and box the man’s ears for him if he hurts you. Or shall you and I set on him, as soon as we’ve got him by himself, and take out all his teeth one after the other? Just to teach him to be a dentist.”

A faint smile began the break through the clouds.

===Chinese===
那次初会之后不久，我便收到她一封迷人的短笺，邀我过些日子去她家吃饭。我高高兴兴地打电话回了谢，因为，说真的，我那时——和今早一样——很想让自己相信，我关于那只画眉之事的解读，是全然错误的。我虽主张，一个人若不喜欢某人，便无权接受其款待，但除了一件事之外，我在每一方面都极其钦佩、极其喜欢罗克夫人，正想摆脱那一桩心事。于是我欣然应邀，随后便匆匆出门，去赴那拖了又拖、令人郁闷的牙医之约。候诊室里有个十二岁光景的女孩，一只手捂着一张愁眉苦脸的小脸，时不时压抑下一声因疼痛或恐惧而起的抽泣。我正琢磨着，想试着去安慰她、或引她分心，会不会不合候诊室的礼数——这时门开了，罗克夫人走了进来。她一见我，便高兴地笑了起来。

「好哇！原来你也是这死囚牢里的一位，」她说，「用不了多久，咱们俩就都要被传去上绞刑架了。我有多胆小，跟你形容你都未必信。咱们怎么就不长一副鸟那样的喙呢？——」

她的目光落到窗边那个愁苦的小小身影上，那张愁苦的脸，那双泪汪汪的眼。

「哎呀，这儿又添了一位咱们这样的，」她说，「亲爱的，他们就这样让你一个人来看牙吗？」

「是——是的。」

「他们也太不像话了！」罗克夫人说，「他们也让我一个人来，我觉得这简直没心肝。可你总不会再孤单了，无论如何，我陪你一起进去，坐在你身边——你要是愿意的话——他要是弄疼了你，我就掴他的耳光。要不，等咱们把他单独逮住了，你我一起扑上去，把他的牙一颗一颗全拔下来，怎么样？也好教他做一回牙医。」

一缕微笑，开始从那阴云之中挣出。

===Original===
“Oh, will you come in with me?” she asked. “I shan’t mind nearly so much, then. It’s﻿—it’s got to come out, you know, and I mayn’t have gas.”

Just the same gleam of a smile as I had seen on Lady Rorke’s face once before quivered there now, a light not of pity, surely.

“Ah, but it won’t ache any more after that,” she said, “and after all, it is so soon over. You’ll just open your mouth as if you were going to put the largest of all strawberries into it, and you’ll hold tight on to my hand, and the dentist takes up something which you needn’t look at﻿—”

There was a want of tact in the vividness of this picture, and the child began to sob again.

“Oh, don’t, don’t!” she cried.

Again the door opened, and she clung to Lady Rorke.

“Oh, I know it’s for me!” she wailed.

Lady Rorke bent over her, scanning her terrified face.

“Come along, my dear,” she said, “and it will be over in no time. You’ll be back here again before this gentleman can count a hundred, and he’ll have all his troubles in front of him still.”

===Chinese===
「哦，你当真陪我进去？」她问，「那样我就不怎么怕了。那颗——那颗牙，你是知道的，非拔不可，又不能用麻气。」

正是我曾一度在罗克夫人脸上见过的那种微笑的微光，此刻又在她脸上颤动着——那决不是怜悯之光。

「啊，可拔掉之后它就再也不会疼了，」她说，「况且，反正一下子就完了。你只管张大嘴，就像要往里头塞一颗最大的草莓那样，再紧紧抓住我的手，然后牙医拿起一样东西——你不必去看它——」

这幅图景未免太栩栩如生，欠了分寸，那孩子又抽泣起来。

「哦，别，别说了！」她叫道。

门又开了，她紧紧偎到罗克夫人身上。

「哦，我知道是叫我了！」她哀声道。

罗克夫人俯下身，端详着那张惊恐的小脸。

「来吧，亲爱的，」她说，「一会儿就完事了。等这位先生数到一百，你就又回到这儿来了，而他那些苦差事，还在前头等着他呢。」

===Original===
Again this morning I tried to expunge from that picture, so trivial and yet so vivid to me, the sinister something which seemed to connect it with the incident about the thrush, and, leaving it, my mind strayed on over other reminiscences of Lady Rorke. Before the season was over I had got to know her well, and the better I knew her the more I marvelled at that many-petalled vitality, which never ceased unfolding itself. She entertained largely, and had that crowning gift of a good hostess, namely, that she enjoyed her own parties quite enormously. She was a very fine horsewoman, and after being up till dawn at some dance, she would be in the Row by half-past eight on a peculiarly vicious mare to whom she seemed to pay only the most cursory attention. She had a good knowledge of music, she dressed amazingly, she was charming to her meagre little husband, playing piquet with him by the hour (which was the only thing, apart from herself, that he cared about), and if in this modern democratic London there could be said to be a queen, there is no doubt who that season would have worn the crown. Less publicly, she was a great student of the psychical and occult, and I remembered hearing that she was herself possessed of very remarkable mediumistic gifts. But to me that was a matter of hearsay, for I never was present at any séance of hers.

===Chinese===
今早我又试着，从这幅画面——于我如此琐碎，又如此鲜明——里抹去那不祥的某物，它似乎把画眉那件事与此事联系了起来；撇下它，我的心便游荡到对罗克夫人的其他追忆上去。那个社交季还没结束，我已和她相当熟稔；我越是了解她，就越惊叹于她那种层层绽放、永无休止的勃勃生机。她款待客人的排场很大，并有着一位好女主人那顶要紧的天赋——即她自己也着实极其享受自己的宴会。她是个极出色的骑手；在某次舞会上彻夜狂舞到天明之后，第二天八点半便会骑着一匹脾气格外暴烈的牝马，出现在骑马道上（the Row），而她对那匹马似乎只投以最敷衍的注意。她颇通音乐，衣着惊人地得体，对她那瘦小枯干的丈夫温柔体贴，陪他一小时一小时地打皮克牌（piquet）——那是除了她本人之外，他唯一在意的事；倘若在这现代民主的伦敦还能说有一位女王，那么那个社交季戴冠冕的是谁，便毫无疑义了。她私下里还是灵学与玄学的热忱研究者，我记得听人说过，她自己便拥有极不寻常的灵媒禀赋。不过于我而言，那只是耳闻，因为我从未出席过她的任何一场降神会。

===Original===
Yet through the triumphant music of her pageant, there sounded, to my ears at least, fragments of a very ugly tune. It was not only in these two instances of its emergence that I heard it, it was chiefly and most persistently audible in her treatment of Archie Rorke, her husband’s cousin. Everyone knew, for none could help knowing, that he was desperately in love with her, and it is impossible to imagine that she alone was ignorant of it. It is, no doubt, the instinct of many women to fan a passion which they do not share, and which they have no intention of indulging, just as the male instinct is to gratify a passion that he does not really feel, but there are limits to mercilessness. She was not “cruel to be kind”; she was kind to be demoniacally cruel. She had him always by her; she gave him those little touches and comrade-like licences which meant nothing to her, but crazed him with thirst; she held the glass close to his lips and then tilted it up and showed it him empty. The more charitable explanation was that she, perhaps, knew that her husband could not live long, and that she intended to marry Archie, and such, so it subsequently appeared, her intentions were. But when I saw her feeding him with husks and putting an empty glass to his lips, nothing, to my mind, could account for her treatment of him except a rapture of cruelty at the sight of his aching. And somehow, awfully and aptly, that seemed to fit in with the affair of the thrush, and the meeting with the forlorn child in the dentist’s waiting-room. Yet ever, through that gruesome twilight, there blazed forth her charm and her beauty and the beam of her joyous vitality, and I would cudgel myself for my nasty interpretations.

===Chinese===
然而，透过她那场庆典般辉煌的乐声，至少在我耳中，总断断续续地响着一支十分难听的调子。我不仅在上述它冒头的两个场合听见过它，它最响、最缠绵不休的，是在她对待阿奇·罗克——她丈夫的表弟——的态度里。人人都知道——谁也没法不知道——他正发狂地爱着她，而很难想象唯独她对此一无所知。许多女人确有一种本能，要去煽动一份她们并不回报、也无意纵容的激情，正如男人的本能是去满足一份他其实并未真正感觉到的激情；但无情的放肆，总该有个限度。她并非“为行善而残酷”；她是“为行恶魔般的残酷而施小恩”。她总把他留在身边；她给他那些小小的亲昵、那种同伴般的不拘小节，那些对她毫无意义的举动，却渴得他发狂；她把杯子端到他唇边，又把它倾翻过来，让他看着那空空的杯底。更宽容些的解释是，她也许知道丈夫命不久长，并有意要嫁给阿奇，而后来事态的走向，她的意图似乎也正是如此。可当我看见她拿麸皮喂他、把一只空杯举到他唇边，那么在我看来，除了看见他痛苦而生出的一种残忍的狂喜之外，再没有什么能解释她对他的所作所为了。而且，不知怎的，既可怕又恰切地，这一节似乎正与画眉那一幕、与牙医候诊室里那个孤苦孩子那一幕严丝合缝。然而在那一片阴森的暮色里，她的魅力、她的美貌、她那勃勃生机的光彩，又始终灼灼地照出来；我便为自己那些刻薄的解读，一再地敲自己的脑袋。

===Original===
It was early in the spring of next year that I was spending a weekend with her and her husband at Lincote. She had suggested my coming down on Saturday morning before the party assembled later in the day, and at lunch I was alone with her husband and her. Sir Ernest was very silent; he looked ill and haggard, and, in fact, hardly spoke a word except when suddenly he turned to the butler and said, “Has anything been heard of the child yet?” He was told that there was no news, and subsided into silence again. I thought that some queer shadow as of suspense or anxiety crossed Lady Rorke’s face at the question; but on the answer, it cleared off again, and, as if to sweep the subject wholly away, she asked me if I could tolerate a saunter with her through the woods till her guests arrived.

Out she came like some splendid Diana of the Forests, and like the goddess’s was the swift, swinging pace of her saunter. Spring all round was riotous in blossom and birdsong; it was just that ecstatic moment of the year when the hounds of spring have run winter to death, and as we gained the high ridge of down above the woods she stopped and threw her arms wide.

===Chinese===
第二年早春，我在林科特和她及其丈夫一起度周末。她建议我在那天晚些时候大批客人到齐之前，星期六一早就先到；于是午饭时，只有我和她夫妇俩在座。厄内斯特爵士沉默寡言；他看上去病恹恹、形容憔悴，事实上，除了有一次突然转身问管家“那孩子可有消息了吗？”之外，几乎一言不发。被告知尚无音讯后，他又归于沉默。我觉得，问到那孩子时，罗克夫人脸上一闪而过某种古怪的阴影，像是期待，又像是忧虑；可一听那回答，阴影便又散去，她像是想把这话头整个儿扫开似的，转而问我，在她那些客人到来之前，可否陪她在林子里随便走走。

她走了出来，俨然一位光辉的林中狄安娜（Diana of the Forests）；她那轻盈的大步，也正如女神那般。四下里，春光在花与鸟的歌中纵情狂欢；那正是一年之中那个心醉神迷的时刻，春天的猎犬已将冬天追杀至死；当我们登上林子上方那道高高的丘陵山脊时，她停下脚步，张开了双臂。

===Original===
“Oh, the sense of spring!” she cried. “The daffodils, and the west wind, and the shadows of the clouds. How I wish I could take the whole lot into my arms and hug them. Miracles are flowering every moment now in the country, while the only miracle in London is the mud. What sunshine, what air! Drink them in, for they are the one divine medicine. One wants that medicine sometimes, for there are sad things and terrible things all round us, pain and anguish, and decay. Yet I suppose that even those call out the splendour of fortitude or endurance. Even when one looks on a struggle which one knows is hopeless, it warms the heart to see it.”

The gleam that shone from her paled, her arms dropped, and she moved on. Then, soft of voice and soft of eye, she spoke again.

“Such a sad thing happened here two days ago,” she said. “A small girl﻿—now what was her name? Yes﻿—Ellen Davenport﻿—brought a note from the village up to the house. I was out, so she left it, and started, it is supposed, to go back home. She has not been seen since. Descriptions of her were circulated in all the villages for miles round; but, as you heard at lunch, there has been no news of her, and the copses and coverts in the park have been searched, but with no result. And yet out of that comes splendour. I went to see her mother yesterday, bowed down with grief, but she won’t give up hope. ‘If it is God’s will,’ she said to me, ‘we shall find my Ellen alive; and if we find her dead, it will be God’s will, too.’ ”

She paused.

“But I didn’t ask you down here to moan over tragedies,” she said. “I wanted you after all your weeks in town to come and have a spring-cleaning. Doesn’t the wind take the dust out of you, like one of those sucking-machines which you put on to carpets? And the sun! Make a sponge of yourself and soak it up till you’re dripping with it.”

===Chinese===
「哦，这春的气息！」她喊道，「水仙花，西风，云影。我真想把这所有一切，一齐拥入怀中、紧紧搂住。如今乡间每时每刻都有奇迹在开花，而伦敦唯一的奇迹，便是烂泥。多好的阳光，多好的空气！把它们饮下去吧，因为它们是唯一的神药。人有时是需要这味药的，因为我们周围尽是些可悲的事、可怕的事，尽是痛苦、煎熬和衰败。然而我想，即便是这些，也能唤起坚忍或忍耐的光辉。哪怕是眼看一场明知无望的挣扎，也会叫人心里发热呢。」

从她身上发出的那道光黯淡了下来，她的双臂垂落，她又往前走去。随后，她声音柔柔的，目光也柔柔的，又开了口。

「就在两天前，这儿发生了一桩很可悲的事，」她说，「一个小女孩——她叫什么来着？哦，是了——艾伦·达文波特（Ellen Davenport）——从村子里送一封信到宅子里来。我不在家，于是她把信留下，据说是动身回家去了。自那以后再没有人见过她。方圆几英里内的各村都散发了她的相貌特征；可正如你午饭时听见的，至今全无音讯；园林里的树丛和灌木丛都搜过了，毫无结果。然而，悲惨之中也有壮美。我昨日去看望她母亲，她悲痛欲绝，却不肯放弃希望。“若是上帝的旨意，”她对我说，“我们定能找到我的艾伦，她还有一口气；若是找到她时她已死了，那也是上帝的旨意。”」

她停了停。

「不过，我请你下乡来，可不是要对着悲剧长吁短叹的，」她说，「我是想让你，在城里待了这许多星期之后，来好好做一场春季的大扫除。这风，不就把你身上的尘土都抽走了吗，就像你铺在地毯上的那种吸尘器？还有这太阳！你把自己化作一块海绵，把这阳光吸个透，吸到浑身都滴出它来。」

===Original===
For a couple of miles, at the least, we kept along this high ridge of down, and the larks were springing from the grass, vocal with song uncongealed, as they aspired and sank again, dropping at last dumb and spent with rapture. Then we descended steeply, through the woods and glades of the park, past thickets of catkinned sallows, and of willows with soft moleskin buttons, and in the hollows the daffodils were dancing, and the herbs of the springtime were pushing up through the brittle withered stuff of the winter. Then, passing along the one street of the red-tiled village, in which my companion pointed me out the house where the poor vanished girl had lived, we turned homewards across the grass and joined the road again at the bottom of the great lake that lies below the terraced gardens of the house.

This lake was artificial, made a hundred years ago by the erection of a huge dam across the dip of the valley, so that the stream which flowed down it was thereby confined and must needs form this sheet of water before it found outlet again through the sluices. At the centre the dam is some twenty-five feet in height, and by the side of the road which crosses it clumps of rhododendrons lean out over the deep water. The margin on the side towards the lake is reinforced with concrete, now mossy and overgrown with herbage, and the face of it, burrows down to the level of the bottom of the dam through four fathoms of dusky water. The lake was high and the overflow poured sonorously through the sluices, and the sun in the west made broken rainbows in the foam of its outpouring.

As we paused there a moment, my companion seemed the incarnation of the sights and sounds that went to the spell of the spring; singing larks and dancing daffodils, west wind and rain-bowed foam and, no less, the dark, deep water, were all distilled into her radiant vitality.

“And now for the house again,” she said, going briskly up the steep slope. “Is it inhospitable of me to wish that no one was coming except, of course, our delightful Archie? A houseful brings London into the country, and we shall talk scandal and stir up mud instead of watching miracles.”

===Chinese===
沿着这道高高的山脊，我们至少走了有两英里；云雀从草丛里腾起，歌声婉转尚未凝结，它们一边扶摇直上、一边又沉落，末了哑然无声、欢欣得力竭而坠。随后我们陡然下行，穿过园林的树林与林间空地，经过一丛丛垂着柔荑花序的黄花柳、和缀着麂皮绒般软纽扣的柳树；洼地里水仙花正翩翩起舞，春天的嫩芽正从冬日那枯脆的败叶中钻出来。接着，我们穿过那个红瓦覆顶的小村唯一的一条街——同伴在那里指给我看那个失踪的可怜女孩住过的房子——便越过草地折回家去，在那座大宅台地花园下方的大湖尽头，又汇入了大路。

这座湖是人工的，一百年前在山谷的洼地里筑起一道巨大的水坝而成；于是顺着山谷流下的那条溪水便被拦起来，非得先汇成这一片水，再从水闸里找到出口不可。水坝中央高约二十五英尺，横过坝顶的那条路旁，一簇簇杜鹃花从深水之上探出身来。朝着湖的那一侧，湖岸以混凝土加固，如今已长满青苔、杂草丛生，而那混凝土的壁面，便穿过四英寻深暗的水，直探到坝底的同一层。湖水满满当当，溢流哗哗地穿过水闸倾泻而下，西斜的太阳，在它溅出的水沫里，映出一段段折断的彩虹。

我们在那儿驻足片刻，我的同伴仿佛是这春之魅力的景象与声响的化身：欢歌的云雀，起舞的水仙，西风，带虹的泡沫，以及那又暗又深的湖水，无不蒸馏进她那光彩照人的勃勃生机里。

「这就回宅子去吧，」她说着，轻快地踏上那段陡坡，「我这念头是不是太失礼了——巴不得除了咱们那位可爱的阿奇，再无别人来？满屋子的客人，等于把伦敦搬到了乡下，我们就只能嚼嚼蜚短流长、搅搅浑水，再也顾不上去看那些奇迹了。」

===Original===
Another faint memory of her lingered somewhere in the dusk, and I groped for it, as one gropes in slime for the roots of a water-plant, and pulled it out. A notorious murderer had been guillotined that morning in France, and in some Sunday paper next day there was a brutal, brilliant, inexcusable little sketch of his being led out between guards for the final scene at dawn outside the prison at Versailles. And, as I wrote my name in Lady Rorke’s visitors’ book on Monday morning, I spilt a blot of ink on the page and hastily had recourse to the blotting-pad on her writing-table in order to minimize the disfigurement. Inside it was this unpardonable picture, cut out and put away, and I thought of the thrush and the dentist’s waiting-room﻿—

A month afterwards her husband died, after three weeks of intolerable torment. The doctor insisted on his having two trained nurses, but Lady Rorke never left him. She was present at the painful dressings of the wound from the operation that only prolonged the misery of his existence, and even slept on the sofa of the room where he lay.

---

===Chinese===
关于她的另一段淡淡的回忆，隐约潜藏在暮色的某处，我摸索着去寻它，像在淤泥里摸索一株水生植物的根一般，把它拽了出来。那天早晨，法国处决了一个声名狼藉的杀人犯，上了断头台；第二天的某份星期日报纸上，登了一幅残忍、精巧、不可原谅的小速写，画的是他在凡尔赛（Versailles）那座监狱外，在两名看守之间被押出来、走向黎明中那最后一幕的情景。而星期一早上，当我在罗克夫人的来客簿上签下名字时，一滴墨水溅落到页面上，我连忙去用她书桌上的吸墨纸，好把污迹减到最小。那吸墨纸里面，正夹着这张不可宽恕的画，剪下来收着，我便想到了那只画眉，想到了牙医的候诊室——

一个月之后，她的丈夫，在三周难以忍受的剧痛折磨后，死去了。医生坚持要给他配两名受过训练的护士，可罗克夫人寸步不离。她亲历了换药时那痛楚的工序——那次手术只拖延了他生存的苦楚；她甚至在病房的沙发上过夜。

---

===Original===
Archie Rorke arrived that evening. He let me know at once that he had seen the announcement of Lady Rorke’s death, and said no more about it till later, when he and I were left alone over the fire in the smoking-room. He looked round to see that the door was shut behind the last bed-goer of my little party, and then turned to me.

“I’ve got to tell you something,” he said. “It’ll take half an hour, so tomorrow will do if you want to be off.”

“But I don’t,” said I.

He pulled himself together from his sprawling sunkenness in his chair.

“Very well,” he said. “What I want to tell you is the story of the breaking-off of my engagement with Sybil. I have often wanted to do so before, but while she was alive, as you will presently see, I could tell nobody. I shall ask you, when you know everything, whether you think I could have done otherwise. And please do not interrupt me till I have finished, unless there is something you don’t understand, for it won’t be very easy to get through with it. But I think I can make it intelligible.”

===Chinese===
那天晚上，阿奇·罗克到了。他立刻便让我知道，他已经看到了罗克夫人去世的讣告，并就此没再多说什么，直到后来，当我和我那小小的一群客人中最后一位就寝者离去后，只剩他和我在吸烟室的炉火前对坐。他四下里看了看，确信身后那扇门在最后一位就寝者身后关上了，这才转向我。

「我有件事得跟你说，」他说，「这要花上半个钟头，所以，你要是想动身，明天再说也成。」

「可我并不想动身。」我说。

他从那张椅子里那瘫软委顿的姿势里，挣扎着坐直了。

「那好，」他说，「我想告诉你的，是我与西比尔解除婚约的始末。从前我常有心想讲给你听，可只要她还活着——这点你马上就会明白——我什么人也不能告诉。等我讲完了这一切，我要问问你，你看我当初除了那样做之外，是否还别有他法。还有，在我讲完之前请别打断我，除非有什么地方你听不明白，因为要把这事讲下去，可不是件容易的事。不过我想，我能把它讲得清楚。」

===Original===
He was silent a moment, and I saw his face working and twitching.

“I must tell somebody,” he said, “and I choose you, unless you mind it awfully. But I simply can’t bear it alone any more.”

“Go on, then, old boy,” I said. “I’m glad you chose me, do you know. And I won’t interrupt.”

Archie spoke.

“A week or two only before our marriage was to have taken place,” he said, “I went down to Lincote for a couple of days. I had had the house done up and redecorated, and now the work was finished and I wanted to see that all was in order. Nothing could be worthy of Sybil, but﻿—well, you can guess, more or less, what my feelings were.

“For a week before there had been very heavy rains, and the lake﻿—you know it﻿—below the garden was very high, higher than I had ever seen it: the water poured over the road across the dam which leads to the village. Under the weight and press of it a great crack had appeared in the concrete with which it is faced, and there was danger of the dam being carried away. If that happened the whole lake would have been suddenly released and no end of damage might have been done. It was therefore necessary to draw off the water as fast as possible to relieve the pressure and repair the crack. This was done by means of big siphons. For two days we had them working, but the crack seemed to extend right to the foundations of the dam, and before it could be repaired all the water in the lake would have to be drawn off. I was just leaving for town, when the foreman came up to the house to tell me that they had found something there. In the ooze and mud at the base of the dam, twenty-five feet below water-level, they had come upon the body of a young girl.”

He gripped the arms of his chair tight. Little did he know that I was horribly aware of what he was going to tell me next.

===Chinese===
他沉默了一会儿，我看见他的脸在抽搐、抖动。

「我总得找个人说一说，」他说，「我选了你，除非你极不愿意听。可这件事，我实在再也无法独自承受下去了。」

「那就说吧，老兄，」我说，「你知道吗，你选了我，我倒挺高兴。我不会打断你的。」

阿奇开了口。

「在我们的婚期之前，只差一两个星期了，」他说，「我到林科特去待两天。宅子我已叫人翻修、重新装饰过，如今工程既已完工，我想去亲自检视一番，看看一切是否妥帖。世上没有什么配得上西比尔的东西，可是——嗳，你多多少少猜得出我当时的心情。

「此前整整一个星期，雨下得极大，花园下面那座湖——你是知道的——涨得极高，比我从前见过的都高：水漫过了通往村子那条越过坝顶的大路。在水压的顶冲之下，坝面那一层混凝土出现了一道大裂缝，整座水坝都有被冲垮的危险。若真那样，整湖的水就会一下子倾泻而下，不知要造成多大的灾祸。因此必须尽快把水排掉，以减轻压力、修补裂缝。这要用几根大虹吸管来做。两天里我们一直让它们工作着，可那裂缝似乎一直延伸到了坝基；在它修补之前，整座湖的水都得排干。我正要动身回城，工头便到宅子里来告诉我，他们在那儿发现了什么东西。在水位以下二十五英尺、水坝底部的淤泥和烂泥里，他们发现了一具年轻女孩的尸体。」

他紧紧攥住椅子的扶手。他全然不知，他接下来要告诉我的，我已骇然料到了。

===Original===
“About a month before my cousin Ernest’s death,” he said, “a mysterious affair happened in the village. A girl named Ellen Davenport had disappeared. She came up one afternoon to the house with a note, and was never seen again, dead or alive. Her disappearance was now explained. A chain of beads round the neck and various fragments of clothing established, beyond any doubt, the identity of what they had found at the bottom of the lake. I waited for the inquest, telegraphing to Sybil that business had detained me, and then returned to town, not intending to tell her what that business was, for our marriage was close at hand and it was not a topic one would choose. She was very superstitious, you know, and I thought that it would shock her. That she would feel it to be unlucky and ill-omened. So I said nothing to her.

“Sybil had extraordinary mediumistic powers. She did not often exercise them and she never would give a séance to anyone she did not know extremely well, for she believed that people brought with them the spiritual influences with which they were surrounded, and that there was the possibility of very evil intelligences being set free. But she had sat several times with me, and I had witnessed some very remarkable manifestations. Her procedure was to put herself, by abstraction of her mind, into a state of trance, and spirits of the dead who were connected with the sitters could then communicate through her. On one occasion my mother, whom she had never seen, and who died many years ago, spoke through her and told me certain facts which Sybil could not have known, and which I did not know. But an old friend of my mother’s, still alive, told me that they were correct. They were of an exceedingly private nature. Sybil also, so she told me, could produce materialisations, but up till now I had never seen any. A remarkable thing about her mediumship was that she would sometimes regain consciousness from her trance while still these communications were being made, and she knew what was going on. She could hear herself speak and be mentally aware of what she was saying. On the occasion, for instance, of which I have told you, when my mother spoke to me she was in this state. The same thing occurred at the sitting of which I shall now speak.

“That night, on my return to London, she and I dined alone. I felt a very strong desire, for which I could not account, that she should hold a sitting﻿—just herself and me﻿—and she consented. We sat in her room, with a shaded lamp, but there was sufficient illumination for me to see her quite distinctly, for her face was towards the light. There was a small table in front of us covered with a dark cloth. She sat close to it, in a high chair, composed herself, and almost immediately went into trance. Her head fell forward and by her slow breathing and her absolute immobility I knew she was unconscious. For a long time we sat there in silence, and I began to think that we should get no manifestations at all, and that the sitting, as sometimes was the case, would be a failure; but then I saw that something was happening.”

===Chinese===
「大约在我表兄厄内斯特去世前一个月，」他说，「村子里发生了一桩离奇的事。一个名叫艾伦·达文波特的女孩失踪了。某天下午她送一封信到宅子里来，此后再没有人见过她，无论死活。如今她的失踪真相大白。一串挂在颈上的珠链和几片衣物残片，确凿无疑地确定了湖底所发现的尸体的身份。我等候死因研讯，同时打电报给西比尔，说有事绊住了我；随后便返回城里，并不打算告诉她那是什么事，因为我们的婚期近在眼前，这不是一个会主动挑选的话题。你是知道的，她极为迷信，我想这会令她震惊。会叫她觉得这不吉利、是不祥之兆。所以我什么也没有对她说。

「西比尔有着异乎寻常的灵媒之力。她不常施展，而且绝不肯为她并非极其熟识的人举行降神会，因为她相信，人们会把环绕自身的灵界影响一同带来，因而有可能放出极恶的灵识。但她已与我一同坐过几次，我亲眼见过一些极不寻常的显现。她的做法是，借由凝神冥想，使自己进入出神状态，于是与在座之人有牵连的亡灵，便能借她之口传话。有一次，我那已去世多年、她从未见过的母亲，借她之口对我说话，告诉了我一些西比尔不可能知道、而我自己也不知道的事实。可我母亲的一位仍在人世的老友告诉我，那些都是真的。它们都属于极其私密的那一类。西比尔也——她对我说——能够引发实体显形，但迄今为止我从未见过。她的灵媒禀赋中有一桩奇特之处：有时，在这些通灵传达还在进行之际，她便会从出神中恢复神志，她知道正在发生的一切。她能听见自己说话，并在心里清清楚楚地意识到自己在说什么。比如，我方才告诉你的我母亲对我说话的那一次，她便是处于这种状态。下面我要说的这次坐关中，也发生了同样的情形。

「那天夜里，回到伦敦之后，只有她和我两个人共进晚餐。我心里生出一种自己也说不清的强烈愿望，希望她能为我举行一场坐关——只她和我两个——她答应了。我们坐在她房里，点着一盏罩着灯罩的灯，但光线足以让我把她看得清清楚楚，因为她的脸朝着光。我们面前摆着一张小桌，铺着一块深色桌布。她紧挨着桌子坐在一张高背椅上，凝神静气，几乎立刻便进了出神状态。她的头垂了下来，从她那徐缓的呼吸和绝对的纹丝不动，我知道她已神志不清。我们就这样默然坐了很久，我开始以为根本不会有什么显现，这次坐关——有时确会如此——将是一场空；可随即我便看见，有什么正在发生。」

===Original===
His hands, with which he gripped the arms of his chair, were trembling. Twice he tried to speak, but it was not till the third attempt that he mastered himself.

“There was forming a mist above the table,” he said. “It was slightly luminous and it spread upwards, pillar-shaped, in height between two and three feet. Then I saw that below the outlying skeins of it something was materialising. It moulded itself into human shape, rising waist-high from the table, and presently shoulders and arms and neck and head were visible, and features began to outline themselves. For some time it remained vague and fluid, swaying backwards and forwards a little; then very quickly it solidified, and there, close in front of me, was the half-figure of a young girl. The eyes were still closed, but now they opened. Round her neck was a chain of beads just such as I had seen laid by the body that had been found in the lake. And then I spoke to her, asking her who she was, though I already knew.

“Her answer was no more than a whisper, but quite distinct.

“Ellen Davenport,” she said.

“A disordered terror seized me. Yet perhaps this little white figure, with its wide-gazing eyes, was some hallucination, something that had no objective existence at all. All day the thought of the poor kiddie whose remains I had seen taken out of the ooze at the bottom of the lake had been vivid in my mind, and I tried to think that what I saw was no more than some strange projection of my thought. And yet I felt it was not so; it was independent of myself. And why was it made manifest, and on what errand had it come? I had pressed Sybil to give me this séance, and God knows what I would have given not to have done so! For one thing I was thankful, namely, that she was in unconscious trance. Perhaps the phantom would fade again before she came out of it.

===Chinese===
他那双紧攥椅子扶手的手，正在发抖。他试着开口，试了两次都没成，到第三次才勉强镇定住自己。

「那张桌子上方，正凝成一团薄雾，」他说，「它微微发光，向上方蔓延，呈一根柱状，高约两三英尺。随后我看见，在它外缘那丝丝缕缕的下方，有什么正在实体化。它塑成了人形，从桌子上方升起齐腰高，不久，双肩、双臂、脖颈和头颅都看得见了，五官也开始显出轮廓。有一阵子它仍是模糊而流动的，稍稍前后摇摆；接着它飞快地凝固起来，就在那儿，离我咫尺之遥，是一个年轻女孩的半截身形。她的双眼还闭着，可此刻睁开了。她颈上挂着一串珠链，与我在湖底发现的那具尸体旁所见的，一模一样。于是我对她说话，问她是谁，尽管我早已知道。

「她的回答不过是一声低语，却十分清晰。

「『艾伦·达文波特，』她说。

「一阵凌乱的恐惧攫住了我。可也许这小小的白色身影，这双圆睁凝视的眼睛，只是某种幻觉，某种根本不具有客观实在的东西。整整一天，我脑子里都鲜活着地想着那可怜的小娃娃——我亲眼看见她的遗骸从湖底的淤泥里被取出来——于是我极力说服自己，我所见的不过是我心思的某种奇异投射。然而我感到并非如此；它是独立于我之外的。可它为什么要显现，又是为何而来呢？是我执意要西比尔为我举行这场降神会的，如今天知道我多么希望当初没这么要求！只有一桩我倒觉得庆幸，那就是她还处在无意识的出神之中。也许那幻影会在我出神之前再度隐去。

===Original===
“And then I heard a stir of movement from the chair where she sat, and, turning, I saw that she had raised her head. Her eyes were open and on her face such a mask of terror as I have never known human being could wear. Recognition was there, too; I saw that Sybil knew who the phantom was.

“The figure that palely gleamed above the table turned its head towards her, and once more the white lips opened.

“Yes, I am Ellen Davenport,” she said.

“The whisper grew louder.

“You might have saved me,” she said, “or you might have tried to save me; but you watched me struggling till I sank.”

“And then the apparition vanished. It did not die away; it was there clear and distinct one moment, at the next it was gone. Sybil and I were sitting alone in her room with the low-burning lamp, and the silence sang in my ears.

“I got up and turned on the switch that kindled the electric lights, and knew that something within me had grown cold and that something had snapped. She still sat where she was, not looking at me at all, but blankly in front of her. She said no word of denial in answer to the terrible accusation that had been uttered. And I think I was glad of that, for there are times when it is not only futility to deny, but blasphemy. For my part, I could neither look at her nor speak to her. I remember holding out my hands to the empty grate, as if there had been a fire burning there. And standing there I heard her rise, and drearily wondered what she would say and knew how useless it would be. And then I heard the whisper of her dress on the carpet and the noise of the door opening and shutting, and when I turned I found that I was alone in the room. Presently I let myself out of the house.”

===Chinese===
「随后，我听见她坐的那张椅子里有一阵动静，转过头去，只见她已经抬起了头。她双眼睁开，脸上带着一副我从未想过人能戴得上的恐怖面具。那里面也有认出；我看见西比尔知道那幻影是谁。

「那张在桌子上方幽幽发光的身形，把头转向她，那双苍白的嘴唇再一次张开。

「『是的，我是艾伦·达文波特，』她说。

「那低语变得更响了。

「『你本可以救我的，』她说，『或者你本可以试着救我；可你却看着我挣扎，直到我沉下去。』

「接着那幻影便消失了。它不是慢慢隐去；上一刻它还清晰分明，下一刻便已不见。西比尔和我单独坐在她的房里，灯焰低燃，那一片静寂在我耳边嗡嗡作响。

「我起身打开电灯的开关，知道我内里有什么已变冷，有什么已经断裂。她仍坐在原处，根本不看我，只是木然地望着前方。对那句已说出口的可怖指控，她没有说半个字的否认。我想，我倒为此感到庆幸，因为有些时候，否认不仅是徒劳，而且是亵渎。至于我，我既不能看她，也不能对她说话。我记得自己朝那空空的炉膛伸出手去，仿佛那里还有一炉火在烧。我就那样站着，听见她站起身，昏昏然想着她会说什么，又深知那将是何等无用。接着我听见她的裙裾在地毯上窸窣，听见门开又门关的声响，待我转过身去，才发现房里只剩我一人。过了一会儿，我自管走出那宅子。」

===Original===
There was a long pause, but I did not break it, for I felt he had not quite finished.

“I had loved her with my whole heart,” he said, “and she knew it. Perhaps that was why I never attempted to see her again and why she did not attempt to see me. That little white figure would always have been with us, for she could not deny the reality of it and the truth of that which it had spoken. That’s my story, then. You needn’t even tell me if you think I could have done differently, for I knew I couldn’t. And she couldn’t.”

He rose.

“I see there is to be an inquest,” he said. “I hope they will find that she killed herself. It will mean, won’t it, that her remorse was unbearable. And that’s atonement.”

He moved towards the door.

“Inscrutable decrees,” he said.

===Chinese===
接着是长长一段沉默，但我没有打破它，因为我感到他还没有完全讲完。

「我曾全心全意地爱过她，」他说，「她知道。也许正因为如此，我从未试图再去找她，她也未试图来找我。那个小小的白色身影，将永远横在我们之间，因为她无法否认它的真实，无法否认它所说的话的真。那么，这就是我的故事了。你甚至不必告诉我，你觉得我当初是否可以另作他法，因为我知道我不能。她也不能。」

他站起身来。

「我看要举行死因研讯了，」他说，「我希望他们裁定她是自尽。那将意味着——是不是？——她的悔恨已无可忍受。而这便是赎罪了。」

他朝门口走去。

「难解的天命。」他说。

## Machaon / 马卡翁

===Original===
I was returning at the close of the short winter day from my visit to St. James's Hospital, where my old servant Parkes, who had been in my service for twenty years, was lying. I had sent him there three days before, not for treatment, but for observation, and this afternoon I had gone up to London, to hear the doctor's report on the case. He told me that Parkes was suffering from an internal tumour, the nature of which could not be diagnosed for certain, but all the symptoms pointed directly to its being cancerous. That, however, must not be regarded as proved; it could only be proved by an exploratory operation to reveal the nature and the extent of the growth, which must then, if possible, be excised. It might involve, so my old friend Godfrey Symes told me, certain tissues and would be found to be inoperable, but he hoped this would not be the case, and that it would be possible to remove it: removal gave the only chance of recovery. It was fortunate that the patient had been sent for examination in an early stage, for thus the chances of success were much greater than if the growth had been one of long standing. Parkes was not, however, in a fit state to stand the operation at once; a recuperative week or ten days in bed was advisable. In these circumstances Symes recommended that he should not be told at once what lay in front of him.

===Chinese===
冬日白昼苦短，天色将暮时我正从圣詹姆斯医院（St. James's Hospital）探视归来——我那服侍了我二十年的老仆帕克斯（Parkes）正躺在那里。三天前我把他送进去，不是为了治疗，而是为了观察，今天下午我便上了伦敦，来听医生对病情的报告。他告诉我，帕克斯患的是一处体内肿瘤，性质尚不能确诊，但一切症状都直指其为癌性。然而这一点尚不能视为定论；唯有施行一次探查性手术，查明这块肿物的性质和范围，方能在可能的情况下将其切除。据我的老友戈弗雷·赛姆斯（Godfrey Symes）说，它也许已侵及某些组织，届时便会发现已无从手术，但他盼着不至如此，盼着还能将它切除：切除是痊愈的唯一机会。所幸病人送来检查时尚在早期，因而成功的把握要比肿物已拖延日久的情况大得多。不过，帕克斯眼下尚非能够立刻经受手术的状态；最好在床上将养一周乃至十日。在这种情形下，赛姆斯建议，不要立刻把等着他的那桩事告诉他。

===Original===
"I can see that he is a nervous fellow," he said, "and to lie in bed thinking of what he has got to face will probably undo all the good that lying in bed will bring to him. You don't get used to the idea of being cut open; the more you think about it, the more intolerable it becomes. If that sort of adventure faced me, I should infinitely prefer not to be told about it until they came to give me the anaesthetic. Naturally, he will have to consent to the operation, but I shouldn't tell him anything about it till the day before. He's not married, I think, is he?"

===Chinese===
「我看得出他是个容易紧张的人，」他说，「让他躺在床上，老想着自己将面临什么，多半会把他卧床将养的好处抵消个干净。人是不会习惯被剖开这种想法的；越想越受不了。换了我要面对这样的事，我宁可一无所知，直等到他们来给我上麻药的那一刻。自然，手术他是非同意不可的，但我不会拖到前一天才把情形告诉他。他没有成家，我想是吧？」

===Original===
"No: he's alone in the world," said I. "He's been with me twenty years."

"Yes, I remember Parkes almost as long as I remember you. But that's all I can recommend. Of course, if the pain became severe, it might be better to operate sooner, but at present he suffers hardly at all, and he sleeps well, so the nurse tells me."

"And there's nothing else that you can try for it?" I asked.

"I'll try anything you like, but it will be perfectly useless. I'll let him have any quack nostrum you and he wish, as long as it doesn't injure his health, or make you put off the operation. There are X-rays and ultraviolet rays, and violet leaves and radium; there are fresh cures for cancer discovered every day, and what's the result? They only make people put off the operation till it's no longer possible to operate. Naturally, I will welcome any further opinion you want."

===Chinese===
「没有：他在这世上举目无亲，」我说，「他跟了我二十年了。」

「是，我记起帕克斯来，几乎和记起你一样久。可我能建议的也就这些了。当然，要是疼得厉害了，早些动手术也许更好，可眼下他几乎一点也不疼，睡得也香，护士是这么告诉我的。」

「除此之外，就没有别的法子可以一试了吗？」我问。

「你愿意试什么都成，可那全无用处。你和他愿意用什么江湖秘方，我都随你们，只要它不伤身子，或者不叫你把手术一拖再拖。X射线、紫外线，紫罗兰叶、镭；每天都有新的治癌法子冒出来，结果又如何？它们不过是叫人把手术一拖再拖，拖到再也动不了手术为止。自然，你还想要谁再来会诊，我也欢迎。」

===Original===
Now Godfrey Symes is easily the first authority on this subject, and has a far higher percentage of cures to his credit than anyone else.

"No, I don't want any fresh opinion," said I.

"Very well, I'll have him carefully watched. By the way, can't you stop in town and dine with me? There are one or two people coming, and among them a perfectly mad spiritualist who has more messages from the other world than I ever get on my telephone. Trunk-calls, eh? I wonder where the exchange is. Do come! You like cranks, I know!"

"I can't, I'm afraid," said I. "I've a couple of guests coming to stay with me today down in the country. They are both cranks: one's a medium."

He laughed.

"Well, I can only offer you one crank, and you've got two," he said. "I must get back to the wards. I'll write to you in about a week's time or so, unless there's any urgency which I don't foresee, and I should suggest your coming up to tell Parkes. Goodbye."

===Chinese===
须知戈弗雷·赛姆斯在这一门上，称得上首屈一指的权威，经他手治愈的比率，远非旁人所能及。

「不，我不要再会诊了。」我说。

「那好，我会让人仔细照看他。对了，你不能在城里留下，跟我吃个饭吗？有一两位客人要来，其中有个十足的疯子灵媒，他从彼世带来的口信，比我电话里接到的还多。长途电话呢，啊？我倒想知道总机在哪里。一定要来呀！我知道你就好些怪人这一口！」

「怕是不能，」我说，「今天有两位客人要下乡来我家小住。两位都是怪人：其中一位是灵媒。」

他笑了起来。

「嗳，我这边只能提供一个怪人，你那里倒有两个，」他说，「我得回病房去了。大约过一周左右我给你写信，除非有什么我预见不到的急事——那时也该由你亲自来把情况告诉帕克斯。再会。」

===Original===
I caught my train at Charing Cross with about three seconds to spare, and we slid clanking out over the bridge through the cold, dense air. Snow had been falling intermittently since morning, and when we got out of the grime and fog of London, it was lying thickly on field and hedgerow, retarding by its reflection of such light as lingered the oncoming of darkness, and giving to the landscape an aloof and lonely austerity. All day I had felt that drowsiness which accompanies snowfall, and sometimes, half losing myself in a doze, my mind crept, like a thing crawling about in the dark, over what Godfrey Symes had told me. For all these years Parkes, as much friend as servant, had given me his faithfulness and devotion, and now, in return for that, all that apparently I could do was to tell him of his plight. It was clear, from what the surgeon had said, that he expected a serious disclosure, and I knew from the experience of two friends of mine who had been in his condition what might be expected of this "exploratory operation." Exactly similar had been these cases; there was clear evidence of an internal growth possibly not malignant, and in each case the same dismal sequence had followed. The growth had been removed, and within a couple of months there had been a recrudescence of it. Indeed, surgery had proved no more than a pruning-knife, which had stimulated that which the surgeon had hoped to extirpate into swifter activity. And that apparently was the best chance that Symes held out: the rest of the treatments were but rubbish or quackery.…

===Chinese===
我在查令十字（Charing Cross）赶上火车，前后只多出了大约三秒钟的余裕，列车便在凛冽浓密的空气里，铿啷作响地滑过铁桥驶出城去。从清早起，雪就断断续续地下着，等我们驶出伦敦的烟尘与大雾，雪已厚厚地盖在田野和树篱上，它那对残光的反照拖延了暮色的降临，使这片风景显出一种冷峻而孤寂的清寒。整整一天，我都感到那种伴雪而生的倦意，有时半入朦胧，我的思绪便像一个在黑暗里摸索爬行的东西，在戈弗雷·赛姆斯告诉我的那些话上缓缓爬过。这些年来，帕克斯半为仆人半为友，将他的忠心与深情悉数付了我，如今作为回报，我所能做的，看来不过是把他的困境说给他听。从外科医生方才所言不难看出，他料定此病凶多吉少，而我从两位有过相同处境的朋友的经历里，也深知这种「探查性手术」之后可能发生什么。那两例的情形与之如出一辙：体内肿物证据确凿，也许并非恶性，然而每一例之后，都跟着同样阴惨的下文。肿物被切除了，可不出两月，它又卷土重来。说到底，外科手术不过是一把修枝的剪刀，反倒把外科医生本想根除的东西，激得越发猖獗起来。而这，看来已是赛姆斯所能开出的最好结局；其余种种疗法，不过是垃圾或江湖把戏罢了……

===Original===
My mind crawled away towards another subject: probably the two visitors whom I expected, Charles Hope and the medium whom he was bringing with him, were in the same train as I, and I ran over in my mind all that he had told me of Mrs. Forrest. It was certainly an odd story he had brought me two days before. Mrs. Forrest was a medium of considerable reputation in psychical circles, and had produced some very extraordinary book-tests which, by all accounts, seemed inexplicable, except on a spiritualistic hypothesis, and no imputation of trickery had, at any rate as yet, come near her. When in trance, she spoke and wrote, as is invariably the case with mediums, under the direction of a certain "control"—that is to say, a spiritual and discarnate intelligence which for the time was in possession of her. But lately there had been signs that a fresh control had inspired her, the nature of which, his name, and his identity was at present unknown. And then came the following queer incident.

===Chinese===
我的心思又慢慢爬向了另一桩事：我所等候的两位客人——查尔斯·霍普（Charles Hope）和他带来的那位灵媒——多半和我同在一班车上，我便在脑中把他先前讲给我听的、关于福雷斯特太太（Mrs. Forrest）的种种又过了一遍。两天前他带来的那个故事，确实颇为古怪。福雷斯特太太在灵学研究圈子里颇有名气，做过一些极其惊人的「书籍测试」——据人所述，那些测试除非以通灵之说来解，似乎无从解释，而且至少到那时为止，丝毫舞弊的嫌疑也不曾沾上她。在出神之际，她和一切灵媒一样，是在某一个「控制灵」（control）的指引下说话、写字的——所谓控制灵，即是一个属灵的、已脱离肉身的智慧体，暂时占据了她的身心。可近来已有迹象表明，一个新的控制灵开始借她显灵，而它的性情、姓名与来历，眼下都还不得而知。于是便有了下面这桩奇事。

===Original===
Last week only when in trance, and apparently under the direction of this new control, she began describing in considerable detail a certain house where the control said that he had work to do. At first the description aroused no association in Charles Hope's mind, but as it went on, it suddenly struck him that Mrs. Forrest was speaking of my house in Tilling. She gave its general features, its position in a small town on a hill, its walled-in garden, and then went on to speak with great minuteness of a rather peculiar feature in the house. She described a big room built out in the garden a few yards away from the house itself at right-angles to its front, and approached by half a dozen stone steps. There was a railing, so she said, on each side of them, and into the railing were twisted, like snake coils, the stems of a tree which bore pale mauve flowers. This was all a correct description of my garden room and the wistaria which writhes in and out of the railings which line the steps. She then went on to speak of the interior of the room. At one end was a fireplace, at the other a big bow-window looking out on to the street and the front of the house, and there were two other windows opposite each other, in one of which was a table, while the other, looking out on to the garden, was shadowed by the tree that twisted itself about the railings. Bookcases lined the walls, and there was a big sofa at right-angles to the fire.…

===Chinese===
就在上个礼拜，她在出神之际，显是在这个新控制灵的指引下，开始相当细致地描述起某一处宅子来，说那控制灵在那里有事要做。起初这一番描述并未在查尔斯·霍普心里勾起任何联想，可说着说着，他猛然省悟：福雷斯特太太所说的，正是我在蒂灵（Tilling）的那幢宅子。她说出了它的大体模样，说它在山上一座小镇里的方位，说它那围了墙的花园，接着便格外细密地讲起这宅子里一处颇为别致的特征。她描述了一间大屋子，建在花园里、离宅子本身几步开外，与宅子正面成直角，要走下六级石阶才能到。她说台阶两边各有栏杆，栏杆里绞着、像蛇盘一般缠着，是一棵开着淡紫花的树的枝茎。这些，全是对我那间花房和缠绕在台阶栏杆间的紫藤（wistaria）的准确写照。她随后又说起屋内的陈设。屋子一头是壁炉，另一头是一扇大弓形窗，朝着街道和宅子正面，另外还有两扇彼此相对的窗，一扇窗下摆着一张桌子，另一扇朝花园，被那缠在栏杆间的树遮得幽幽的。书柜沿墙排开，与壁炉成直角处摆着一张大沙发……

===Original===
Now all this, though it was a perfectly accurate description of a place that, as far as could be ascertained, Mrs. Forrest had never seen, might conceivably have been derived from Charles Hope's mind, since he knew the room well, having often stayed with me. But the medium added a detail which could not conceivably have been thus derived, for Charles believed it to be incorrect. She said that there was a big piano near the bow-window, while he was sure that there was not. But oddly enough I had hired a piano only a week or so ago, and it stood in the place that she mentioned. The control then repeated that there was work for him to do in that house. There was some situation or complication there in which he could help, and he could "get through" better (that is, make a clearer communication) if the medium could hold a séance there. Charles Hope then told the control that he believed he knew the house that he had been speaking of, and promised to do his best. Shortly afterwards Mrs. Forrest came out of trance, and, as usual, had no recollection of what had passed.

===Chinese===
虽说这一切——尽管它对一个就所能查知、福雷斯特太太从未到过的地方描述得毫厘不差——未尝不可以视作取自查尔斯·霍普心中，因为他常来我家小住，对那间屋子知之甚详。然而灵媒又添了一个细节，这细节断无从如此取来，因为查尔斯相信它是不对的。她说弓形窗旁摆着一架大钢琴，而他确信那里并没有。可奇就奇在，大约一周前我才租来一架钢琴，正摆在她所说的位置上。那控制灵便重复道，在那宅子里有事等他去做。那里头有某种处境或纠葛，他能从中相助，而且倘若灵媒能在那里举办一场降神会，他便能「更清楚地传达」（即是说，做出更明白的沟通）。查尔斯·霍普于是告诉那控制灵，他想他认得它所说的那宅子，并答应尽力而为。不久福雷斯特太太便出了神，一如往常，对刚才所发生的一切毫无记忆。

===Original===
So Charles came to me with the story exactly as I have given it here, and though I could not think of any situation or complication in which an unknown control of a medium I had never seen could be of assistance, the whole thing (and in especial that detail about the piano) was so odd that I asked him to bring the medium down for a sitting or a series of sittings. The day of their arrival was arranged, but when three days ago Parkes had to go into hospital, I was inclined to put them off. But a neighbour away for a week obligingly lent me a parlourmaid, and I let the engagement stand. With regard to the situation in which the control would be of assistance, I can but assure the reader that as far as I thought about it at all, I only wondered whether it was concerned with a book on which I was engaged, which dealt (if I could ever succeed in writing it) with psychical affairs. But at present I could not get on with it at all. I had made half a dozen beginnings which had all gone into the wastepaper basket.

===Chinese===
于是查尔斯带着这个故事来找我，原原本本如我这里所述，虽说我想不出有任何处境或纠葛，能让一个我素未谋面的灵媒手下一个来历不明的控制灵插得上手；可整件事（尤其是关于钢琴的那个细节）实在太古怪了，我便请他把那灵媒请下乡来，做一场、或一连几场降神会。他们到访的日子既已议定，可三天前帕克斯又不得不进了医院，我便有心把约会推迟。所幸一位出门一周的邻居热心肠地把她的客厅女佣借给了我，我便让这约会照旧。至于那控制灵能施以援手的处境究竟是什么，我只能向读者保证：就我对此上心的程度而言，我只不过在想，它是否与我手头所写的那本书有关——那本书（倘若我当真能写成的话）谈的正是灵学之事。可眼下我全然写不下去。已开了六七个头，统统进了字纸篓。

===Original===
My guests proved not to have come by the same train as I, but arrived shortly before dinnertime, and after Mrs. Forrest had gone to her room, I had a few words with Charles, who told me exactly how the situation now stood.

"I know your caution and your captiousness in these affairs," he said, "so I have told Mrs. Forrest nothing about the description she gave of this house, or of the reason why I asked her to come here. I said only, as we settled, that you were a great friend of mine and immensely interested in psychical affairs, but a country-mouse whom it was difficult to get up to town. But you would be delighted if she would come down for a few days and give some sittings here."

"And does she recognise the house, do you think?" I asked.

"No sign of it. As I told you, when she comes out of trance she never seems to have the faintest recollection of what she has said or written. We shall have a séance, I hope, tonight after dinner."

"Certainly, if she will," said I. "I thought we had better hold it in the garden-room, for that was the place that was so minutely described. It's quite warm there, central-heating and a fire, and it's only half a dozen yards from the house. I've had the snow swept from the steps."

===Chinese===
我的客人原来并不与我同车，但在晚餐前不大一会儿便到了，福雷斯特太太上她房间去之后，我和查尔斯谈了几句，他把眼下情形原原本本告诉了我。

「我知道你在这类事上谨慎而挑剔，」他说，「所以我丝毫没有向福雷斯特太太提起她所说的这宅子的描述，也没说起我请她来此的缘由。我只照我们议定的那样说：你是我的一位至交，对灵学之事极有兴趣，却是一只难以请进城来的乡下鼠。可倘若她肯下乡来住几天，在这里做几场降神会，你便会十分欢喜。」

「那么你想，她认得出这宅子吗？」我问。

「毫无迹象。我跟你说过，她一出神，对所说过、所写过的东西似乎便再无半点记忆。今晚晚餐之后，我希望我们能办一场降神会。」

「自然，倘若她愿意。」我说，「我想我们最好在花房里办，因为被描述得那样细致的，正是那个地方。那里头挺暖和，有暖气，也有火炉，离宅子不过六码之遥。我已叫人把台阶上的雪扫了。」

===Original===
Mrs. Forrest turned out to be a very intelligent woman, well spiced with humour, gifted with a sane appreciation of the comforts of life, and most agreeably furnished with the small change of talk. She was inclined to be stout, but carried herself with briskness, and neither in body nor mind did she suggest that she was one who held communication with the unseen: there was nothing wan or occult about her. Her general outlook on life appeared to be rather materialistic than otherwise, and she was very interesting on the topic when, about halfway through dinner, the subject of her mediumship came on the conversational board.

"My gifts, such as they are," she said, "have nothing to do with this person who sits eating and drinking and talking to you. She, as Mr. Hope may have told you, is quite expunged before the subconscious part of me—that is the latest notion, is it not?—gets into touch with discarnate intelligences. Until that happens, the door is shut, and when it is over, the door is shut again, and I have no recollection of what I have said or written. The control uses my hand and my voice, but that is all. I know no more about it than a piano on which a tune has been played."

"And there is a new control who has lately been using you?" I asked.

She laughed.

"You must ask Mr. Hope about that," she said. "I know nothing whatever of it. He tells me it is so, and he tells me—don't you, Mr. Hope?—that he hasn't any idea who or what the new control is. I look forward to its development; my idea is that the control has to get used to me, as in learning a new instrument. I assure you I am as eager as anyone that he should gain facility in communication through me. I hope, indeed, that we are to have a séance tonight."

===Chinese===
福雷斯特太太原来是位十分聪慧的女子，言语里颇带几分机趣，对世间种种舒服受用有着健康而不失分的鉴赏，闲谈时所费的零碎小钱，也最是令人如沐春风。她身段偏丰腴，举止却利落得很，无论身心都不像是一个与冥冥中物相通的人：她身上既无惨淡之色，也无玄秘之气。她对人生的一般看法，与其说是超脱的，不如说是相当唯物的；晚餐吃到一半，当她的灵媒身份被搬上餐桌的话题时，她那一番话倒颇可玩味。

「我这点本事，」她说，「与这个正坐着又吃又喝、又与你们说话的人，并无干系。她——正如霍普先生也许已告诉过你的——在我那潜意识的一部分（这是最新的说法，不是吗？）与那些脱离肉身的智慧相通之前，便已被抹去了。在那发生之前，门是关着的；事过之后，门又关上了，而对于我说过、写过的东西，我一无所记。那控制灵用的是我的手、我的嗓子，仅此而已。我对它的事知道得，并不比一架被人弹过一支曲子的钢琴更多。」

「而近来正有一个新的控制灵借你显灵？」我问。

她笑了起来。

「这个你可得问霍普先生了，」她说，「我对此一无所知。他告诉我是这样，他又告诉我——是不是呀，霍普先生？——他也弄不清这新控制灵究竟是谁、是什么。我倒盼着看它如何发展；依我看，控制灵得慢慢与我磨合，就好比学习弹奏一件新乐器。我向你保证，对于它能借着我越发娴熟地传达信息，我和旁人一样急切盼着呢。我真希望，今晚我们能办一场降神会。」

===Original===
The talk veered again, and I learned that Mrs. Forrest had never been in Tilling before, and was enchanted with the snowy moonlit glance she had had of its narrow streets and ancient residences. She liked, too, the atmosphere of the house: it seemed tranquil and kindly; especially so was the little drawing-room where we had assembled before dinner.

I glanced at Charles.

"I had thought of proposing that we should sit in the garden-room," I said, "if you don't mind half a dozen steps in the open. It adjoins the house."

"Just as you wish," she said, "though I think we have excellent conditions in here without going there."

===Chinese===
话锋又转，我得知福雷斯特太太从未到过蒂灵，对她月下雪中所瞥见的那些窄巷古宅，颇为神往。她也喜欢这宅子的氛围：宁静而和煦；尤其是饭前我们聚在一起的那间小客厅。

我瞟了查尔斯一眼。

「我原想提议，我们到花房里坐，」我说，「倘若你不介意在露天空地走那六级台阶。它紧挨着宅子。」

「随你的便，」她说，「不过我看，我们在这里头的条件已极好，不必非去那儿不可。」

===Original===
This confirmed her statement that she had no idea after she had come out of trance what she had said, for otherwise she must have recognised at the mention of the garden-room her own description of it, and when soon after dinner we adjourned there, it was clear that, unless she was acting an inexplicable part, the sight of it twanged no chord of memory. There we made the very simple arrangements to which she was accustomed.

As the procedure in such sittings is possibly unfamiliar to the reader, I will describe quite shortly what our arrangements were. We had no idea what form these manifestations—if there were any—might take, and therefore we, Charles and I, were prepared to record them on the spot. We three sat round a small table about a couple of yards from the fire, which was burning brightly; Mrs. Forrest seated herself in a big armchair. Exactly in front of her on the table were a pencil and a block of paper in case, as often happened, the manifestation took the form of automatic script—writing, that is, while in a state of trance. Charles and I sat on each side of her, also provided with pencil and paper in order to take down what she said if and when (as lawyers say) the control took possession of her. In case materialised spirits appeared, a phenomenon not as yet seen at her séances, our idea was to jot down as quickly as possible whatever we saw or thought we saw. Should there be rappings or movements of furniture, we were to make similar notes of our impressions. The lamp was then turned down, so that just a ring of flame encircled the wick, but the firelight was of sufficient brightness, as we tested before the séance began, to enable us to write and to see what we had written. The red glow of it illuminated the room, and it was settled that Charles should note by his watch the time at which anything occurred. Occasionally, throughout the séance a bubble of coal-gas caught fire, and then the whole room started into strong light. I had given orders that my servants should not interrupt the sitting at all, unless somebody rang the bell from the garden-room. In that case it was to be answered. Finally, before the séance began, we bolted all the windows on the inside and locked the door. We took no other precautions against trickery, though, as a matter of fact, Mrs. Forrest suggested that she should be tied into her chair. But in the firelight any movement of hers would be so visible that we did not adopt this precaution. Charles and I had settled to read to each other the notes we made during the sitting, and cut out anything that both of us had not recorded. The accounts, therefore, of this sitting and of that which followed next day are founded on our joint evidence. The sitting began.

===Chinese===
这倒印证了她所说的：出了神之后，对自己所言便一无所知——否则，一提到花房，她必会认出那正是她自己描述过的地方；而饭后不久我们移步到那里时，看得分明，除非她在演一出无从解释的戏，否则那地方的景象并未拨动她记忆的任何一根弦。在那里，我们按她所习以为常的，做了些再简单不过的安排。

降神会的程序，读者也许并不熟悉，我便简要地描述一下我们的布置。我们并不知道这些显灵——倘若当真有的话——会取何种形式，因而查尔斯和我都做好了当场记录的准备。我们三人围一张小桌而坐，离熊熊燃烧的炉火约有两码远；福雷斯特太太坐在一张大扶手椅里。桌上正对着她的，是一支铅笔和一沓拍纸簿，以防显灵取了自动书写的形式——即在出神之中提笔写字，这也是常有的事。查尔斯和我分坐她两侧，也各备纸笔，以便在控制灵（借用法律行话来说）倘若、一旦占据她时，把她口中所说逐字记下。倘若有物质化灵体显现——这是她的降神会上还从未见过的现象——我们的打算是，尽快把所见或自以为所见的一切潦草记下。若是有叩击声或家具的挪动，我们也照样把印象记下。随后把灯捻小，只余灯芯上一圈火焰，但炉火的光已足够明亮——这一点我们在降神会开始之前先试过了——能让我们写得下字、也看得清所写。炉火的红光把屋子照得通红，又议定但凡有什么事发生，查尔斯便按表记下时辰。整场降神会中，偶尔有一团煤气气泡燃着了，于是整间屋子陡然亮起一阵强光。我已吩咐下人，除非有人从花房按铃，否则绝不可前来打搅；若按了铃，则须应门。最后，降神会开始之前，我们把所有窗户从里头插上，把门锁好。其余防伪的措施一概未取，虽说福雷斯特太太其实提议过把她绑在椅子上。但在炉火的映照下，她一举一动都无所遁形，我们便不采这一项预防。查尔斯和我议定，会后将各自所记的笔记互相对读，凡两人都未记下的内容便剔除。因此，本篇对这场降神会、以及次日那一场的记述，皆以我们两人共同的证词为据。降神会开始了。

===Original===
Mrs. Forrest was leaning back at ease with her eyes open and her hands on the arms of her chair. Then her eyes closed and a violent trembling seized her. That passed, and shortly afterwards her head fell forward and her breathing became very rapid. Presently that quieted to normal pace again, and she began to speak at first in a scarcely audible whisper and then in a high shrill voice, quite unlike her usual tones.

I do not think that in all England there was a more disappointed man than I during the next half-hour. "Starlight," it appeared, was in control, and Starlight was a personage of platitudes. She had been a nun in the time of Henry VII, and her work was to help those who had lately passed over. She was very busy and very happy, and was in the third sphere where they had a great deal of beautiful music. We must all be good, said Starlight, and it didn't matter much whether we were clever or not. Love was the great thing; we had to love each other and help each other, and death was no more than the gate of life, and everything would be tremendously jolly.… Starlight, in fact, might be better described as claptrap, and I began thinking about Parkes.…

===Chinese===
福雷斯特太太舒舒服服地仰靠着，双目微睁，两手搁在扶手上。继而双目合拢，一阵剧烈的颤抖攫住了她。这一阵过去，不多时她的头便垂了下来，呼吸变得十分急促。不久又平静下来，恢复如常，她开始说话，起初低得几乎听不见，像是耳语，随后则是又高又尖的嗓音，与她平素的声调判若两人。

接下来的半个钟头里，我想全英国再没有比我更失望的人了。原来当值的是「星光」（Starlight），而星光是个满口陈词滥调的角色。她说她曾在亨利七世（Henry VII）年间做过修女，她的职司是扶助新近亡故的人。她很忙，也很快乐，住在第三重天界，那里有许多美妙的音乐。她说我们大家都要做善人，聪明不聪明倒不打紧。爱才是头等大事；我们要彼此相爱，彼此扶助，而死亡不过是生命之门，一切都一定会很好很好……一言以蔽之，「星光」不如称作「套话」，我便开始想帕克斯的事去了……

===Original===
And then I ceased to think about Parkes, for the shrill moralities of Starlight ceased, and Mrs. Forrest's voice changed again. The stale facility of her utterance stopped and she began to speak, quite unintelligibly, in a voice of low baritone range. Charles leaned across the table and whispered to me.

"That's the new control," he said.

The voice that was speaking stumbled and hesitated: it was like that of a man trying to express himself in some language which he knew very imperfectly. Sometimes it stopped altogether, and in one of these pauses I asked:

"Can you tell us your name?"

There was no reply, but presently I saw Mrs. Forrest's hand reach out for the pencil. Charles put it into her fingers and placed the writing-pad more handily for her. I watched the letters, in capitals, being traced. They were made hesitatingly, but were perfectly legible. "Swallow," she wrote, and again "Swallow," and stopped.

"The bird?" I asked.

The voice spoke in answer; now I could hear the words, uttered in that low baritone voice.

"No, not a bird," it said. "Not a bird, but it flies."

===Chinese===
可随即我便不再想帕克斯了，因为星光那一套尖声尖气的训诫戛然而止，福雷斯特太太的嗓音又变了。那一种烂熟而流利的腔调停了下来，她开始说话，吐字含混难辨，嗓音是低低的男中音。查尔斯隔着桌子探过身来，对我耳语。

「这是那个新控制灵。」他说。

那说话的声音磕磕绊绊、欲言又止：像一个人正努力用他所知甚少的某种语言来表达自己。有时它索性全然噤了声，趁其中一次停顿，我问道：

「你能把你的名字告诉我们吗？」

没有回答，但不多时我便看见福雷斯特太太的手伸向了那支铅笔。查尔斯把它放进她指间，又把拍纸簿挪得更顺手些。我看着一个一个大写字母被描了出来，落笔虽迟疑，却十分清楚。她写的是「燕」（Swallow），又写了一遍「燕」，便停下了。

「是那种鸟吗？」我问。

那声音开口作答；这一回我听得清字句了，用的便是那低低的男中音。

「不，不是鸟，」它说，「不是鸟，可它会飞。」

===Original===
I was utterly at sea; my mind could form no conjecture whatever as to what was meant. And then the pencil began writing again. "Swallow, swallow," and then with a sudden briskness of movement, as if the guiding intelligence had got over some difficulty, it wrote "Swallowtail."

This seemed more abstrusely senseless than ever. The only connection with swallowtail in my mind was a swallowtailed coat, but whoever heard of a swallowtailed coat flying?

"I've got it," said Charles. "Swallowtail butterfly. Is it that?"

There came three sudden raps on the table, loud and startling. These raps, I may explain, in the usual code mean "Yes." As if to confirm it the pencil began to write again, and spelled out "Swallowtail butterfly."

"Is that your name?" I asked.

There was one rap, which signifies "No," followed by three, which means "Yes." I had not the slightest idea of what it all signified (indeed it seemed to signify nothing at all), but the sitting had become extraordinarily interesting if only for its very unexpectedness. The control was trying to establish himself by three methods simultaneously—by the voice, by the automatic writing, and by rapping. But how a swallowtail butterfly could assist in some situation which was now existing in my house was utterly beyond me.… Then an idea struck me: the swallowtail butterfly no doubt had a scientific name, and that we could easily ascertain, for I knew that there was on my shelves a copy of Newman's *Butterflies and Moths of Great Britain*, a sumptuous volume bound in morocco, which I had won as an entomological prize at school. A moment's search gave me the book, and by the firelight I turned up the description of this butterfly in the index. Its scientific name was *Papilio machaon*.

"Is Machaon your name?" I asked.

The voice came clear now.

"Yes, I am Machaon," it said.

===Chinese===
我如坠五里雾中；任凭我怎样揣度，也猜不出这话是什么意思。这时铅笔又开始写了。「燕，燕，」接着，笔锋忽地一转，像是那个在指引的智慧体克服了某种难处，写下「燕尾」（Swallowtail）二字。

这可比方才更加深奥而无谓了。「燕尾」在我脑中唯一的关联，是一件燕尾服，可谁曾听说一件燕尾服会飞呢？

「我明白了，」查尔斯说，「燕尾蝶。是这个吗？」

桌上猛地传来三下叩击，又响又惊人。这三下叩击，我可以说明一下，按通行的暗码是「是」的意思。像是为了印证似的，铅笔又开始写，拼出「燕尾蝶」（Swallowtail butterfly）几个字。

「那是你的名字吗？」我问。

一下叩击，意为「否」，紧接着三下，意为「是」。这一切究竟有何含义，我丝毫也摸不着头脑（事实上似乎全无含义可言），可单凭这一份出乎意料，这场降神会也已变得分外有趣起来。那控制灵正以三种法子同时确立自己的身份——以嗓音，以自动书写，又以叩击。可一只燕尾蝶怎么能在我的宅子里眼下某种处境中助上一臂之力，我却全然想不通……这时我忽然心生一计：燕尾蝶想必有一个学名，那是不难查到的，因为我知道我书架上有一本纽曼（Newman）所著的《大不列颠的蝶与蛾》（*Butterflies and Moths of Great Britain*），摩洛哥皮精装的一卷豪华本，是我在学校里所得的昆虫学奖品。片刻翻检便找到了那本书，借着炉火我在索引里翻到这蝴蝶的描述。它的学名是 *Papilio machaon*（金凤蝶）。

「马卡翁（Machaon）是你的名字吗？」我问。

那声音这一回清清楚楚。

「是的，我是马卡翁。」它说。

===Original===
With that came the end of the séance, which had lasted not more than an hour. Whatever the power was that had made Mrs. Forrest speak in that male voice and struggle, through that roundabout method of "swallow, swallowtail, Machaon," to establish its identity, it now began to fail. Mrs. Forrest's pencil made a few illegible scribbles, she whispered a few inaudible words, and presently with a stretch and a sigh she came out of trance. We told her that the name of the control was established, but apparently Machaon meant nothing to her. She was much exhausted, and very soon I took her across to the house to go to bed, and presently rejoined Charles.

"Who was Machaon, anyhow?" he asked. "He sounds classical: more in your line than mine."

I remembered enough Greek mythology to supply elementary facts, while I hunted for a particular book about Athens.

"Machaon was the son of Asclepios," I said, "and Asclepios was the Greek god of healing. He had precincts, hydropathic establishments, where people went to be cured. The Romans called him Aesculapius."

"What can he do for you then?" asked Charles. "You're fairly fit, aren't you?"

===Chinese===
降神会到此便告终了，前后不过一小时光景。那究竟是怎样一股力量，借福雷斯特太太的口说出男声，又那样迂回曲折地、经由「燕、燕尾、马卡翁」的法子来确立自己的身份——它如今开始衰竭了。福雷斯特太太的铅笔潦草地涂了几下，看不分明，她又低声说了几句听不清的话，不多时便伸个懒腰、叹一口气，出了神。我们告诉她控制灵的名字已经定了下来，可「马卡翁」对她显然毫无意义。她疲惫得很，不久我便送她回宅子里就寝，又回头来与查尔斯会合。

「马卡翁到底是谁呢？」他问，「听着像是古典人物：是你的本行，不是我的。」

我的希腊神话倒还记得一些，足以供些基本的史料，一面又去翻一本谈雅典的书。

「马卡翁是阿斯克勒庇俄斯（Asclepios）的儿子，」我说，「而阿斯克勒庇俄斯是希腊的医神。他有神苑，有水疗的院所，人们到那里求医。罗马人叫他埃斯枯拉庇乌斯（Aesculapius）。」

「那他能为你做什么呢？」查尔斯问，「你倒挺康健的，不是吗？」

===Original===
Not till he spoke did a light dawn on me. Though I had been thinking so much of Parkes that day, I had not consciously made the connection.

"But Parkes isn't," said I. "Is that possible?"

"By Jove!" said he.

I found my book, and turned to the accounts of the precinct of Asclepios in Athens.

"Yes, Asclepios had two sons," I said—"Machaon and Podaleirios. In Homeric times he wasn't a god, but only a physician, and his sons were physicians too. The myth of his godhead is rather a late one—"

I shut the book.

"Best not to read any more," I said. "If we know all about Asclepios, we shall possibly be suggesting things to the medium's mind. Let's see what Machaon can tell us about himself, and we can verify it afterwards."

===Chinese===
直到他这一开口，我方才恍然大悟。那一天我虽满脑子都是帕克斯，却从未有意识地把它联系起来。

「可帕克斯并不康健。」我说，「这可能吗？」

「天哪！」他说。

我找到了那本书，翻到关于雅典阿斯克勒庇俄斯神苑的记载。

「是的，阿斯克勒庇俄斯有两个儿子，」我说——「马卡翁和波达勒里俄斯（Podaleirios）。在荷马时代他还不是神，不过是个医师，他的儿子们也是医师。他身为神祇的神话是较晚才兴起的——」

我把书合上。

「最好别再往下看了，」我说，「我们若把阿斯克勒庇俄斯的事知道得太全，只怕反倒会给灵媒的心里头下暗示。且看马卡翁能就他自己告诉我们些什么，之后我们再去一一查证。」

===Original===
It was therefore with no further knowledge than this on the subject of Machaon that we proposed to hold another séance the next day. All morning the bitter air had been laden with snow, and now the street in front of my house, a byway at the best in the slender traffic of the town, lay white and untrodden, save on the pavement where a few passengers had gone by. Mrs. Forrest had not appeared at breakfast, and from then till lunchtime I sat in the bow-window of the garden-room, for the warmth of the central heating, of which a stack of pipes was there installed, and for securing the utmost benefit of light that penetrated this cowl of snow-laden sky, busy with belated letters. The drowsiness that accompanies snowfall weighed heavily on my faculties, but as far as I can assert anything, I can assert that I did not sleep. From one letter I went on to another, and then for the sixth or seventh time I tried to open my story. It promised better now than before, and searching for a word that would not come to my pen, I happened to look up along the street which lay in front of me. I expected nothing: I was thinking of nothing but my work; probably I had looked up like that a dozen times before, and had seen the empty street, with snow lying thickly on the roadway.

===Chinese===
于是，对于马卡翁的事，我们所知不过如此，便打算次日再办一场降神会。整整一上午，凛冽的空气里都饱含着雪意，此刻我家门前的那条街——即使在小镇本就稀疏的车马里，也不过是一条僻径——白皑皑地、杳无人迹地铺展开去，只有人行道上留下几位行人走过的脚印。福雷斯特太太没有下楼用早饭，从那时直到午饭时分，我便坐在花房那扇弓形窗下——为的是集中暖气，那一带正装着一排暖气片，也为多沾一些穿透这重重雪天的一些天光——手忙脚乱地料理积压的信件。伴雪而生的那种困倦沉沉地压在我的神思上，但凡是能由我断言的，我都可以断言我并未睡着。一封信接一封信，写完之后，我又第六次、抑或第七次地试着给我的故事开个头。它这回的情形倒比方才顺利些了，正为一个笔下不来的词犯难，我无意间抬起头，朝面前的街道望了望。我并不期待什么：我所想的不过是手头的活计；大约先前我也这样抬过十来回头，所见的不过是一条空街，路面上厚厚地铺着雪。

===Original===
But now the roadway was not untenanted. Someone was walking down the middle of it, and his aspect, incredible though it seemed, was not startling. Why I was not startled I have no idea: I can only say that the vision appeared perfectly natural. The figure was that of a young man, whose hair, black and curly, lay crisply over his forehead. A large white cloak reaching down to his knees enveloped him, and he had thrown the end of it over his shoulder. Below his knees his legs and feet were bare, so too was the arm up to the elbow, with which he pressed his cloak to him, and there he was walking briskly down the snowy street. As he came directly below the window where I sat, he raised his head and looked at me directly, and smiled. And now I saw his face: there was the low brow, the straight nose, the curved and sunny mouth, the short chin, and I thought to myself that this was none other than the Hermes of Praxiteles, he whose statue at Olympia makes all those who look on it grow young again. There, anyhow, was a boyish Greek god, stepping blithely and with gay, incomparable grace along the street, and raising his face to smile at this stolid, middle-aged man who blankly regarded him. Then with the certainty of one returning home, he mounted the steps outside the front door, and seemed to pass into and through it. Certainly he was no longer in the street, and, so real and solid-seeming had he been to my vision, that I jumped up, ran across the few steps of garden, and went into the house, and I should not have been amazed if I had found him standing in the hall. But there was no one there, and I opened the front door: the snow lay smooth and untrodden down the centre of the road where he had walked and on my doorstep. And at that moment the memory of the séance the evening before, about which up till now I had somehow felt distrustful and suspicious, passed into the realm of sober fact, for had not Machaon just now entered my house, with a smile as of recognition on some friendly mission?

===Chinese===
可这会儿，那路面上并不是空无一人。有人正顺着路中央走来，而他的形相——虽说匪夷所思——却并不叫人惊惧。我为何不惊惧，自己也说不上来：我只能说的是，那景象显得自然而然。那身影是个青年男子，一头乌黑的卷发，紧贴贴地搭在额前。一袭白色的大氅直盖到膝下，将他裹住，他随手把大氅的一角甩到肩上。膝盖以下，腿脚都赤裸着；那只将大氅拢在身上的手臂，也赤裸到肘部——他便这样大踏步地走在雪中的街上。待他正走到我所坐的窗下，便抬起头来直直地望着我，微微一笑。这时我看清了他的脸：低低的额，挺直的鼻，弧线温柔而带阳光气的嘴，短短的下巴。我心下暗想，这分明便是普拉克西特列斯（Praxiteles）所雕的赫耳墨斯（Hermes）——那尊立在奥林匹亚（Olympia）的雕像，凡看见它的人都会顿觉青春重来。无论如何，一位少年模样的希腊神祇，正踏着欢快的、妙不可言的飘逸风姿，沿着街走来，又抬起脸，对着这个呆呆望着他的、中年木讷的男子微笑。随后，他带着一个归人那种理所当然的笃定，登上前门外的台阶，仿佛穿过那扇门走了进去。街上的确已不见他的人影，而他的身影在我的注视下又那样真切、那样仿佛触手可及，于是我霍地起身，跑过那几步花园，冲进宅子里——即便我发现他正立在门厅里，我也不会多么惊讶。可那里空无一人，我又推开大门：路的中央——他所走过的那段——和我家门阶上，雪都平平整整，未受践踏。也正是在这一刻，昨夜那场降神会的记忆——直到方才我还莫名其妙地怀着几分疑虑——便落入了不容置疑的事实之列：因为方才走进我这宅子的，岂不正是马卡翁？脸上带着一个朋友来访、似有相识的微笑，是为一桩友好的使命而来。

===Original===
We sat again that afternoon by daylight, and now, I must suppose, the control was more actively and powerfully present, for hardly had Mrs. Forrest passed into trance than the voice began, louder than it had been the night before, and far more distinct. He—Machaon I must call him—seemed to be anxious to establish his identity beyond all doubt, like some newcomer presenting his credentials, and he began to speak of the precinct of Asclepios in Athens. Often he hesitated for a word in English, often he put in a word in Greek, and as he spoke, fragments of things I had learned when an archaeological student in Athens came back into my mind, and I knew that he was accurately describing the portico and the temple and the well. All this I toss to the sceptic to growl and worry over and tear to bits; for certainly it seems possible that my mind, holding these facts in its subconsciousness, was suggesting them to the medium's mind, who thereupon spoke of them and, conveying them back to me, made me aware that I had known them.… My forgotten knowledge of these things and of the Greek language came flooding back on me, as he told us, now half in Greek, and half in English, of the patients who came to consult the god, how they washed in the sacred well for purification, and lay down to sleep in the portico. They often dreamed, and in the interpretation of their dreams, which they told to the priest next day, lay the indication of the cure. Or sometimes the god healed more directly, and accompanied by the sacred snake walked among the sleepers and by his touch made them whole. His temple was hung with ex-votos, the gifts of those whom he had cured. And at Epidaurus, where was another shrine of his, there were great mural tablets recording the same.…

===Chinese===
那天下午我们在天光之下又坐了一场，而这一回，想必那控制灵是在场得更强劲、更有力了，因为福雷斯特太太才一入神，那嗓音便响了起来，比前一夜更响，也分明得多。他——我不得不称他为马卡翁了——似乎急切地要把自己的身份坐实，毫无疑义，像一个新来乍到的人出示他的凭证；他于是说起雅典的阿斯克勒庇俄斯神苑来。他时常为一个英文词犯难，时常夹杂一个希腊词；他这一开口，我当年在雅典做考古学生时所学的种种零碎便一一涌回脑中，我知道他所描述的那柱廊、那神庙、那口井，分毫不错。这一切，我尽可抛给怀疑者去龇牙咧嘴、撕咬挑剔；因为诚然有可能，是我的心，将这些事实压在潜意识里，又暗示给了灵媒的心，她便据此说了出来，再传回给我，使我相信自己是知道的……他对我们讲述那些前来求医的人如何而来，如何在圣泉里沐浴洁身，如何在柱廊里躺下入眠——这些被我遗忘了的知识，对那些事、对希腊文的记忆，都潮水一般涌回我身上，他说来半是希腊文、半是英文。他们常常做梦，而治病的线索，便落在对那些梦的解说之中——次日他们把梦讲给祭司听，由祭司来圆解。又或者，有时医神更直接地施治，他在圣蛇的陪伴下走入酣睡者之间，只一触，便使他们痊愈。他的神庙里挂满了还愿的供品，都是他所治愈的人所献上的。而在埃皮达鲁斯（Epidaurus）——那里有他的另一处圣苑——墙上镶着巨大的铭匾，记的也是同样的事……

===Original===
Then the voice stopped, and as if to prove identity by another means, the medium drew the pencil and paper to her, and in Greek characters, unknown apparently to her, she traced the words "Machaon, son of Asclepios.…

There was a pause, and I asked a direct question, which now had been long simmering in my mind.

"Have you come to help me about Parkes?" I asked. "Can you tell me what will cure him?"

The pencil began to move again, tracing out characters in Greek. It wrote *φέγγος ξ*, and repeated it. I did not at once guess what it meant, and asked for an explanation. There was no answer, and presently the medium stirred, stretched herself and sighed, and came out of trance. She took up the paper on which she had written.

"Did that come through?" she asked. "And what does it mean? I don't even know the characters.…

Then suddenly the possible significance of *φέγγος ξ* flashed on me, and I marvelled at my slowness. *φέγγος*, a beam of light, a ray, and the letter *ξ*, the equivalent of the English *x*. That had come in direct answer to my question as to what would cure Parkes, and it was without hesitation or delay that I wrote to Symes. I reminded him that he had said that he had no objection to any possible remedy, provided it was not harmful, being tried on his patient, and I asked him to treat him with X-rays. The whole sequence of events had been so frankly amazing, that I believe the veriest sceptic would not have done otherwise than I did.

===Chinese===
随后那嗓音停了下来，像是要另用一种法子来证实身份，灵媒把铅笔和纸拉到自己面前，用她显然并不认得的希腊文字母，描下「马卡翁，阿斯克勒庇俄斯之子」几个字……

停了一停，我开口直问，这个问题在我心里已熬了许久了。

「你是为帕克斯的事来助我的吗？」我问，「你能告诉我，什么能治好他？」

铅笔又开始动起来，描出一串希腊文。它写的是 *φέγγος ξ*，又重复了一遍。我一时没有猜出它的意思，便请它解释。没有回答，不多时灵媒动了动，伸个懒腰，叹一口气，出了神。她拿起自己写过的那张纸。

「这是通出来的吗？」她问，「这是什么意思？我连这些字母都不认得……」

猛然间，*φέγγος ξ* 的可能含义在我脑中一闪而过，我奇怪自己怎会这样迟钝。*φέγγος*，一束光，一道射线；而字母 *ξ*，正与英文的 *x* 相当。这是对我「什么能治好帕克斯」之问的直接作答，于是我毫不迟疑、毫不耽搁地给赛姆斯写了信。我提醒他，他曾说过，只要无害，任何可能的疗法他都不反对在他病人身上一试，我便请他用X射线来治。这整件事的来龙去脉实在太过惊人，我相信最不肯轻信的人，处我之地也会作同样的处置。

===Original===
Our sittings continued, but after this day we had no further evidence of this second control. It looked as if the intelligence (even the most incredulous will allow me, for the sake of convenience, to call that intelligence Machaon) that had described this room, and told Mrs. Forrest that he had work to do here, had finished his task. Machaon had said, or so my interpretation was, that X-rays would cure Parkes. In justification of this view it is proper to quote from a letter which I got from Symes a week later.

===Chinese===
我们的降神会仍在继续，可那一天之后，我们再没有这位第二控制灵的任何证据。看情形，那个描述过这间屋子、并告诉福雷斯特太太他在这里有活要干的智慧体（即便最不肯轻信的人，为方便起见，想必也会容许我把那智慧体称作马卡翁），已经完成了他的差事。马卡翁说过——至少我是这样解读的——X射线能治好帕克斯。为给这一看法作证，理当摘引一封我一星期后从赛姆斯处收到的信。

===Original===
> "There is no need for you to come up to break to Parkes that an operation lies in front of him. In answer to your request, and without a grain of faith in its success, I treated him with X-rays, which I assured you were useless. Today, to speak quite frankly, I don't know what to think, for the growth has been steadily diminishing in size and hardness, and it is perfectly evident that it is being absorbed and is disappearing.
> "The treatment through which I put Parkes is that of ————. Here in this hospital we have had patients to whom it brought no shadow of benefit. Often it had been continued on these deluded wretches till any operation which might possibly have been successful was out of the question owing to the encroachment of the growth. But from the first dose of the X-rays, Parkes began to get better, the growth was first arrested, and then diminished.
> "I am trying to put the whole thing before you with as much impartiality as I can command. So, on the other side, you must remember that Parkes's was never a proved case of cancer. I told you that it could not be proved till the exploratory operation took place.
