“‘Are you there?’ he said.

“There was no reply, of course, and he asked it again. This time there came a rap like that which I had thought during dinner to be the postman. But whether it was that the room was dark, or that despite myself I felt rather excited too, it seemed to me now to be far louder than before. Also it appeared to come neither from here nor there, but to be diffused through the room.

“Then the curious revolving of the table ceased, but the intense, violent throbbing continued. My eyes were fixed on it, though owing to the darkness I could see nothing, when quite suddenly a little speck of light moved across it, so that for an instant I saw my own hands. Then came another and another, like the spark of matches struck in the dark, or like fireflies crossing the dusk in southern gardens. Then came another knock of shattering loudness, and the throbbing of the table ceased, and the lights vanished.

===Chinese===
说话间屋里便已一片漆黑，只余炉火一丝极淡的微光。窗帘很厚，街上的灯光透不进来，行人车辆那熟悉而热闹的声响传进来时也变得隐隐约约。我站在桌子靠门那一侧；路易斯与我对面而立，因为借着那将熄未熄的炉火光晕，我能看见他身影隐约的轮廓。

「把手放在桌上，」他说，「要很轻，并且——怎么说好呢——期待着。」

我心里虽仍在抗议，却依言期待着。我听见他的呼吸略略加快了，而我心想，竟有人能站在黑暗里、俯身在一张大红木桌上方期待着，并从中寻得兴奋，这也未免古怪。忽然——我那轻轻搭在桌面上的指尖，开始感到一阵隐隐的震颤，再没有比水壶里的水刚开始沸腾时、从壶柄传来的那种震颤更与之相像的了。这震颤渐渐变得明显、剧烈，直到像一辆汽车的引擎在悸动。它仿佛发出一个低沉的嗡嗡声。随后，十分突兀地，桌子好像从我手指底下溜了出去，开始非常缓慢地旋转。

「手别离开它，跟着它动。」路易斯说，说话间我看见他的身影从炉火前移开了，随着桌子一同移动。

有片刻的静默，我们颇有些可笑地继续绕着圈子，可以说是与桌子同步移动。随后路易斯又开口了，他的声音兴奋得发颤。

「你在吗？」他说。

当然没有回应，于是他又问了一遍。这一回，响起了一下叩击声，与我吃饭时以为是邮差的那一下如出一辙。但不知是因为屋里黑，还是因为我不由得也感到几分兴奋，此刻听来它仿佛比先前响亮得多。而且，它似乎既不从这儿、也不从那儿传来，而是弥漫在整间屋子里。

接着，桌子那古怪的旋转停止了，可那强烈、剧烈的悸动仍在继续。我的两眼盯着它，尽管由于黑暗我什么也看不见——便在此时，一个极小的光点掠过桌面，使我有一瞬间看见了自己的双手。接着又是一个、又一个，如同在黑暗中划着的火柴迸出的火星，又如同南国庭园里掠过暮色的萤火。随后又是震耳欲聋的一声叩击，桌子的悸动停止了，那些光点也消失了。

===Original===
“Such were the phenomena at the first séance at which I was present, but Fielder, it must be remembered, had been studying, ‘expecting,’ he called it, for some years. To adopt spiritualistic language (which at that time I was very far from doing), he was the medium, I merely the observer, and all the phenomena I had seen that night were habitually produced or witnessed by him. I make this limitation since he told me that certain of them now appeared to be outside his own control altogether. The knockings would come when his mind, as far as he knew, was entirely occupied in other matters, and sometimes he had even been awakened out of sleep by them. The lights were also independent of his volition.

“Now my theory at the time was that all these things were purely subjective in him, and that what he expressed by saying that they were out of his control, meant that they had become fixed and rooted in the unconscious self, of which we know so little, but which, more and more, we see to play so enormous a part in the life of a man. In fact, it is not too much to say that the vast majority of our deeds spring, apparently without volition, from this unconscious self. All hearing is the unconscious exercise of the aural nerve, all seeing of the optic, all walking, all ordinary movement seem to be done without the exercise of will on our part. Nay more, should we take to some new form of progression, skating, for instance, the beginner will learn with falls and difficulty the outside edge, but within a few hours of his having learned his balance on it, he will give no more thought to what he learned so short a time ago as an acrobatic feat, than he gives to the placing of one foot before the other.

“But to the brain specialist all this was intensely interesting, and to the student of hypnotism, as I was, even more so, for (such was the conclusion I came to after this first séance), the fact that I saw and heard just what Louis saw and heard was an exhibition of thought-transference which in all my experience in the Charcot-schools I had never seen surpassed, if indeed rivalled. I knew that I was myself extremely sensitive to suggestion, and my part in it this evening I believed to be purely that of the receiver of suggestions so vivid that I visualised and heard these phenomena which existed only in the brain of my friend.

===Chinese===
这便是我在场的第一场降神会（séance）上所出现的种种异象，但必须记住，菲尔德已研究了——他称之为「期待」——好些年。借用通灵术的术语（那时我离接受这些术语还差得远），他是灵媒（medium），我不过是观察者；那一夜我所见的种种异象，都是他平日便能唤出、或常常见到的。我作此限定，是因为他告诉我，其中某些现象如今看来，已完全不在他的掌控之内。那些叩击声会在他——就他所知——心思完全放在别的事情上时响起，有时他甚至会被它们从睡眠中惊醒。那些光点，亦不依他的意志为转移。

我当时的见解是：这一切都纯粹是他自身的主观产物，而他所谓「不在自己掌控之内」，意思则是这些现象已固定、扎根于那个无意识自我（unconscious self）之中——我们对这无意识自我所知甚少，却越来越看清它在一个人的一生中扮演着何等重大的角色。事实上，可以毫不夸张地说：我们所做的事，绝大多数都看似不经意地从这个无意识自我中涌出。一切听觉，都是听觉神经的无意识运作；一切视觉，都是视神经的无意识运作；一切行走，一切寻常的动作，仿佛都不经我们意志的运用而完成。更有甚者，纵使我们染指某种全新的移动方式——比方说滑冰——初学者要在外刃上稳住平衡，必得跌摔连连、苦不堪言；可一旦他在外刃上找到了平衡，不出几个钟头，他对这么短时间之前还视若杂技绝技的那一点本事，便不再多费一分心思，正如他不再费心思该如何把一只脚迈到另一只脚前面一样。

但对于一位脑科专家而言，这一切都无比引人入胜；而对于我这样一个催眠术的研究者来说，就更是如此。因为（这便是我在第一场降神会之后所得的结论）：我之所见所闻，正与路易斯之所见所闻完全一致，这是一种思想传递（thought-transference）的展现，而在我于沙尔科学派（Charcot-schools）所积累的全部经验中，我从未见过能与之媲美的，更遑论超越。我深知自己极易受暗示，而这一晚上我所扮演的角色，我相信纯粹是暗示接收者的角色——那些暗示生动到了这般地步，使我看见、听见了这些其实只存在于我朋友脑中的异象。

===Original===
“We talked over what had occurred upstairs. His view was that the Thing was trying to communicate with us. According to him it was the Thing that moved the table and tapped, and made us see streaks of light.

“‘Yes, but the Thing,’ I interrupted, ‘what do you mean? Is it a great-uncle—oh, I have seen so many relatives appear at séances, and heard so many of their dreadful platitudes—or what is it? A spirit? Whose spirit?’

“Louis was sitting opposite to me, and on the little table before us there was an electric light. Looking at him I saw the pupil of his eye suddenly dilate. To the medical man—provided that some violent change in the light is not the cause of the dilation—that meant only one thing, terror. But it quickly resumed its normal proportion again.

“Then he got up, and stood in front of the fire.

===Chinese===
我们上楼之后，把方才发生的事议论了一番。他的看法是：那个东西正试图与我们沟通。照他说，是那个东西推动了桌子、敲出叩击声，并让我们看见了那一道道光丝。

「不错，可那个东西，」我插嘴道，「你指的是什么？是某位伯祖父吗——嗐，降神会上我见过的亲戚太多了，听过的他们那种可怕的陈词滥调也太多了——还是什么？一个亡灵？谁的亡灵？」

路易斯坐在我对面，我们面前的小桌上放着一盏电灯。我看着他，只见他的瞳孔猛然放大。对一名医生而言——除非光线的剧烈变化是瞳孔放大的原因——这只意味着一件事：恐惧。可瞳孔很快又恢复了正常的比例。

随后他站起身，走到炉火前。

===Original===
“‘No, I don’t think it is great-uncle anybody,’ he said, ‘I don’t know, as I told you, what the Thing is. But if you ask me what my conjecture is, it is that the Thing is an Elemental.’

“‘And pray explain further. What is an Elemental?’

“Once again his eye dilated.

“‘It will take two minutes,’ he said. ‘But, listen. There are good things in this world, are there not, and bad things? Cancer, I take it is bad, and—and fresh air is good; honesty is good, lying is bad. Impulses of some sort direct both sides, and some power suggests the impulses. Well, I went into this spiritualistic business impartially. I learned to “expect,” to throw open the door into the soul, and I said, “Anyone may come in.” And I think Something has applied for admission, the Thing that tapped and turned the table and struck matches, as you saw, across it. Now the control of the evil principle in the world is in the hands of a power which entrusts its errands to the things which I call Elementals. Oh, they have been seen; I doubt not that they will be seen again. I did not, and do not ask good spirits to come in. I don’t want “The Church’s one foundation” played on a musical box. Nor do I want an Elemental. I only threw open the door. I believe the Thing has come into my house, and is establishing communication with me. Oh, I want to go the whole hog. What is it? In the name of Satan, if necessary, what is it? I just want to know.’

===Chinese===
「不，我不认为它是哪位的伯祖父，」他说，「我已告诉过你，我不知道那东西是什么。可你若问我我的猜测，那么我猜，那个东西是一个元素精（Elemental）。」

「那么请进一步解释。何谓元素精？」

他的瞳孔又是一下放大。

「这要花两分钟，」他说，「不过，你听着。这世上有善的东西，不是吗，也有恶的东西？我想，癌是恶的，而——而新鲜空气是善的；诚实是善的，撒谎是恶的。某种冲动指引着这两面，而某种力量在授意着这些冲动。好吧，我是不偏不倚地涉足这通灵术一行的。我学会了『期待』，学会了把通往灵魂的门敞开，我说：『谁都可以进来。』而我相信，已经有某个东西申请入内了——就是那个敲出叩击声、转动桌子、并在桌面上划火柴的东西，你都看见了。世上恶之原则的掌控权，握在某一种力量手中，而这力量把它的一些差事，交托给我所说的那些元素精。哦，它们是被人看见过的；我毫不怀疑，它们还会再被看见。我并未——也并不——请善灵进来。我可不想听人家用八音盒奏《教会的唯一根基》。我也并不『想要』一个元素精。我只不过是敞开了那扇门。我相信那个东西已经进了我的宅子，正在与我建立联系。哦，我要一查到底。它究竟是什么？必要时，凭撒旦之名，它是什么？我只想知道。」

===Original===
“What followed I thought then might easily be an invention of the imagination, but what I believed to have happened was this. A piano with music on it was standing at the far end of the room by the door, and a sudden draught entered the room, so strong that the leaves turned. Next the draught troubled a vase of daffodils, and the yellow heads nodded. Then it reached the candles that stood close to us, and they fluttered, burning blue and low. Then it reached me, and the draught was cold, and stirred my hair. Then it eddied, so to speak, and went across to Louis, and his hair also moved, as I could see. Then it went downwards towards the fire, and flames suddenly started up in its path, blown upwards. The rug by the fireplace flapped also.

“‘Funny, wasn’t it?’ he asked.

“‘And has the Elemental gone up the chimney?’ said I.

“‘Oh, no,’ said he, ‘the Thing only passed us.’

“Then suddenly he pointed at the wall just behind my chair, and his voice cracked as he spoke.

“‘Look, what’s that?’ he said. ‘There on the wall.’

===Chinese===
接下来发生的事，我当时觉得极易出自想象的编造，但我相信确曾发生的是这样：屋子那一头靠门处摆着一架钢琴，上头摆着乐谱，一阵突来的穿堂风刮进屋里，竟强到能把乐谱的书页翻动。紧接着，这阵风又搅扰了一只插着黄水仙的花瓶，那黄色的花冠便纷纷点动。随后它刮到了我们近旁的烛火，烛焰便摇曳起来，烧得低而发蓝。接着它刮到了我身上，这阵风冰凉，掀动了我的头发。然后，可以这么说，它打了个旋，折向路易斯那一边，我看见他的头发也随之而动。随后它向下扑向炉火，火焰便在它经过之处突然腾起，朝上窜着。壁炉前的地毯也拍动起来。

「挺好玩，是不是？」他问。

「那么这元素精是顺着烟囱走了？」我说。

「哦，不，」他说，「那东西只是从我们身边经过。」

随后他猛地指向我椅子正后方的那堵墙，说话时嗓音都发了劈。

「瞧，那是什么？」他说，「在墙上。」

===Original===
“Considerably startled I turned in the direction of his shaking finger. The wall was pale grey in tone, and sharp-cut against it was a shadow that, as I looked, moved. It was like the shadow of some enormous slug, legless and fat, some two feet high by about four feet long. Only at one end of it was a head shaped like the head of a seal, with open mouth and panting tongue.

“Then even as I looked it faded, and from somewhere close at hand there sounded another of those shattering knocks.

“For a moment after there was silence between us, and horror was thick as snow in the air. But, somehow neither Louis or I were frightened for more than one moment. The whole thing was so absorbingly interesting.

“‘That’s what I mean by its being outside my control,’ he said. ‘I said I was ready for any—any visitor to come in, and by God, we’ve got a beauty.’

===Chinese===
我相当吃惊地顺着他发抖的手指转过头去。那堵墙是浅灰色的，映在其上轮廓分明的，是一道——我看着的时候——动了动的影子。它像某种巨大蛞蝓的影子，无足而肥硕，约莫两英尺高、四英尺长。只不过它的一端有个脑袋，形状像海豹的头，张着嘴，伸着喘息的舌头。

就在我看着的时候，它褪去了；而从近旁某处，又响起了震耳欲聋的一声叩击。

随后我俩之间静默了片刻，恐怖如雪一般在空气中浓稠密布。可不知怎的，不论是路易斯还是我，都不过惊恐了那么一瞬。整件事实在太引人入胜了。

「这便是我所谓它不在我的掌控之内，」他说，「我说过，任何——任何来客我都准备让它进来，而老天，这下我们可请来了一位了不得的。」

===Original===
“Now I was still, even in spite of the appearance of this shadow, quite convinced that I was only taking observations of a most curious case of disordered brain accompanied by the most vivid and remarkable thought-transference. I believed that I had not seen a slug-like shadow at all, but that Louis had visualised this dreadful creature so intensely that I saw what he saw. I found also that his spiritualistic trash-books which I thought a truer nomenclature than textbooks, mentioned this as a common form for Elementals to take. He on the other hand was more firmly convinced than ever that we were dealing not with a subjective but an objective phenomenon.

===Chinese===
此时我仍——纵然那影子已经现身——坚信自己不过是在观察一个极其离奇的大脑错乱病例，并伴之以异常生动、异常惊人的思想传递。我相信自己根本未曾看见什么蛞蝓状的影子，只不过是路易斯把这可怖的生物想象得过于强烈，以至于我看见了他所看见的。我还发现，他的那些通灵术废书——我以为这个名字比「教科书」更贴切——里头提到，这种形态正是元素精常取的形态。他则正相反，比从前更加坚信：我们所对付的，并非主观的现象，而是客观的现象。

===Original===
“For the next six months or so we sat constantly, but made no further progress, nor did the Thing or its shadow appear again, and I began to feel that we were really wasting time. Then it occurred to me, to get in a so-called medium, induce hypnotic sleep, and see if we could learn anything further. This we did, sitting as before round the dining-room table. The room was not quite dark, and I could see sufficiently clearly what happened.

“The medium, a young man, sat between Louis and myself, and without the slightest difficulty I put him into a light hypnotic sleep. Instantly there came a series of the most terrific raps, and across the table there slid something more palpable than a shadow, with a faint luminance about it, as if the surface of it was smouldering. At the moment the medium’s face became contorted to a mask of hellish terror; mouth and eyes were both open, and the eyes were focused on something close to him. The Thing waving its head came closer and closer to him, and reached out towards his throat. Then with a yell of panic, and warding off this horror with his hands, the medium sprang up, but It had already caught hold, and for the moment he could not get free. Then simultaneously Louis and I went to his aid, and my hands touched something cold and slimy. But pull as we could we could not get it away. There was no firm handhold to be taken; it was as if one tried to grasp slimy fur, and the touch of it was horrible, unclean, like a leper. Then, in a sort of despair, though I still could not believe that the horror was real, for it must be a vision of diseased imagination, I remembered that the switch of the four electric lights was close to my hand. I turned them all on. There on the floor lay the medium, Louis was kneeling by him with a face of wet paper, but there was nothing else there. Only the collar of the medium was crumpled and torn, and on his throat were two scratches that bled.

“The medium was still in hypnotic sleep, and I woke him. He felt at his collar, put his hand to his throat and found it bleeding, but, as I expected, knew nothing whatever of what had passed. We told him that there had been an unusual manifestation, and he had, while in sleep, wrestled with something. We had got the result we wished for, and were much obliged to him.

“I never saw him again. A week after that he died of blood-poisoning.

===Chinese===
此后大约六个月，我们频频地坐着尝试，却毫无新的进展，那东西也罢、它的影子也罢，都不曾再出现，我渐觉我们其实是在白费时辰。这时我想到一个法子：请一位所谓的灵媒进来，诱导其进入催眠的睡眠，看我们能否探得更多的东西。我们便这么做了，仍像从前那样围坐在餐室的桌前。屋里并不全黑，所发生的一切我都能看得相当清楚。

那灵媒是个年轻人，坐在我和路易斯之间，我毫不费力地便让他进入了轻度的催眠睡眠。霎时间便响起一连串极其可怕的叩击声，而顺着桌面滑过来一样比影子更具实感的东西，它周身带着一层淡淡的光晕，仿佛它的表面正在阴燃。与此同时，那灵媒的脸扭曲成了一副地狱般惊恐的面具；嘴和眼都大张着，两眼定定地盯着离他很近的某样东西。那东西挥动着它的头，离他越来越近，伸向他的喉咙。那灵媒发出一声惊惶的尖叫，双手招架着这可怖的东西，纵身跳了起来，可那东西已经攥住了他，一时之间他挣不脱身。接着路易斯和我同时扑上去救他，我的双手触到了一样又冷又黏的东西。可无论我们怎么拽，都拽不开。它无处可以牢牢抓紧；仿佛你想抓住一撮黏滑的毛皮，而那触感可怖、不洁，有如麻风病人。随后，在某种绝望之中——尽管我仍无法相信这可怖之物是真实的，因为这必然是病态想象的幻象——我想起那四盏电灯的开关就在我手边。我把它们一齐拧亮。地板上躺着那位灵媒，路易斯跪在他身旁，脸白得像一张湿纸，但屋里别无他物。只有那灵媒的衣领皱作一团、被撕破了，他喉头上有两道渗着血的抓痕。

那灵媒仍在催眠的睡眠之中，我便把他唤醒。他摸了摸衣领，把手放到喉头，发觉在流血；可正如我所料，他对刚才发生的事一无所知。我们告诉他，方才出现了一场异乎寻常的显灵，他在睡梦中与某样东西搏斗了一番。我们已得到了想要的结果，对他万分感激。

我再也没见过他。一周之后，他死于败血症。

===Original===
“From that evening dates the second stage of this adventure. The Thing had materialised (I use again spiritualistic language which I still did not use at the time). The huge slug, the Elemental, manifested itself no longer by knocks and waltzing tables, nor yet by shadows. It was there in a form that could be seen and felt. But it still—this was my strong point—was only a thing of twilight; the sudden kindling of the electric light had shown us that there was nothing there. In this struggle perhaps the medium had clutched his own throat, perhaps I had grasped Louis’ sleeve, he mine. But though I said these things to myself, I am not sure that I believed them in the same way that I believe the sun will rise tomorrow.

“Now as a student of brain-functions and a student in hypnotic affairs, I ought perhaps to have steadily and unremittingly pursued this extraordinary series of phenomena. But I had my practice to attend to, and I found that with the best will in the world, I could think of nothing else except the occurrence in the hall next door. So I refused to take part in any further séance with Louis. I had another reason also. For the last four or five months he was becoming depraved. I have been no prude or Puritan in my own life, and I hope I have not turned a Pharisaical shoulder on sinners. But in all branches of life and morals, Louis had become infamous. He was turned out of a club for cheating at cards, and narrated the event to me with gusto. He had become cruel; he tortured his cat to death; he had become bestial. I used to shudder as I passed his house, expecting I knew not what fiendish thing to be looking at me from the window.

“Then came a night only a week ago, when I was awakened by an awful cry, swelling and falling and rising again. It came from next door. I ran downstairs in my pyjamas, and out into the street. The policeman on the beat had heard it too, and it came from the hall of Louis’ house, the window of which was open. Together we burst the door in. You know what we found. The screaming had ceased but a moment before, but he was dead already. Both jugulars were severed, torn open.

===Chinese===
这场历险的第二阶段，便从那天晚上算起。那东西已经实体化了（我再次借用通灵术的术语，那时我仍不接受这些术语）。那巨大的蛞蝓、那元素精，已不再以叩击声和跳舞的桌子、也不再以影子来显现。它已在那里，以一种可看可触的形态。但它仍——这是我有力的一句——不过是个半明半暗之物；电灯骤然亮起时已向我们显示，那里什么也没有。在那场搏斗中，也许是灵媒自己攥住了自己的喉咙，也许是我抓住了路易斯的袖子、他抓住了我的。可尽管我嘴上这么对自己说，我是否也像相信太阳明天会升起那样相信这些话，却不好说。

如今，作为一名大脑机能的研究者、一名催眠术的研究者，我也许本该孜孜不倦地追查这一连串异乎寻常的现象。可我有我的诊务要料理，而我发觉，就算怀着世上最殷切的心思，除了隔壁厅堂里发生的事，我也无法再想别的。于是我拒绝再与路易斯同坐任何降神会。我还有一个理由。在过去四五个月里，他日渐堕落。我平生既非道学先生，也非清教徒，我也希望我未曾向罪人露出过法利赛人式（Pharisaical）的冷肩。可无论是在生活还是道德的方方面面，路易斯都已变得臭名昭著。他因打牌作弊被一家俱乐部开除，竟还津津有味地把这事讲给我听。他变得残忍，把他那只猫折磨至死；他变得如同禽兽。我每从他的宅子门前经过，都不由得打个寒噤，预感不知什么恶魔般的东西正从窗口瞪着我。

接着便到了仅在一周之前的一个夜晚——我被一声可怕的叫声惊醒：那叫声时而高涨、时而低落、复又高昂。声音来自隔壁。我穿着睡衣奔下楼，冲到街上。巡逻的警察也听见了，声音是从路易斯那宅子的厅堂里传出的，那扇窗正开着。我们合力把门撞开。你们知道我们发现了什么。那惨叫不过片刻之前才止住，可他已经死了。两根颈静脉都已被切断，被撕裂开来。

===Original===
“It was dawn, early and dusky when I got back to my house next door. Even as I went in something seemed to push by me, something soft and slimy. It could not be Louis’ imagination this time. Since then I have seen glimpses of it every evening. I am awakened at night by tappings, and in the shadows in the corner of my room there sits something more substantial than a shadow.”

===Chinese===
我回到隔壁自家屋里时，天已破晓，是那种早而昏蒙的微光。就在我进门的当儿，似乎有什么东西从我身边挤了过去，又软又黏。这一回，总不可能是路易斯的想象了吧。从那以后，每天傍晚我都瞥见它的一斑半爪。夜里我常被一阵阵叩击声惊醒，而我屋里角落的阴影中，坐着一样比影子更具实感的东西。

===Original===
Within an hour of my leaving Dr. Assheton, the quiet street was once more aroused by cries of terror and agony. He was already dead, and in no other manner than his friend, when they got into the house.

===Chinese===
我离开阿什顿医生不到一个钟头，那条安静的街道便再度被恐惧和痛苦的叫声所惊动。等到人们进得屋内，他早已死去，死法与他那位朋友如出一辙。
